title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
在昔成周以鄉三物教萬民
鄉大夫掌鄉政令而鄉吏各
教其所治三年攷其德行道
藝賢者能者莫不興起嚮用
我
國家弘文崇道三歲開科天下
===
守臣各掄鄉之俊升之禮部
寔成周制云嘉靖二十有八
年復當鄉試巡按廣東監察
御史陳策樹聲明紀損益章
程一時人文煥然丕振時提
督巡撫兵部右侍郎歐陽必
進揆文奮武奠綏南服申戒
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

在昔成周，以鄉三物教萬民，鄉大夫掌鄉政令，而鄉吏各教其所治。三年攷其德行道藝，賢者能者莫不興起嚮用。我國家弘文崇道，三歲開科，天下守臣各掄鄉之俊，升之禮部，寔成周制云。

嘉靖二十有八年，復當鄉試。巡按廣東監察御史陳策樹聲明紀，損益章程，一時人文煥然丕振。時提督巡撫兵部右侍郎歐陽必進揆文奮武，奠綏南服，申戒
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In ancient times, the Zhou taught all the people through the three categories of township instruction. The township grand officers administered township government and ordinances, while the township officials each instructed those under their jurisdiction. Every three years, they assessed their virtue, conduct, learning, and skills; all those of worth and ability were brought forward and employed. Our dynasty promotes letters and honors the Way, holding examinations every three years. Throughout the realm, the officials governing the territories select the outstanding men of their respective localities and send them onward to the Ministry of Rites. This is indeed the system of the Zhou.

In the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing [1549], the Provincial Examination was again due to be held. Chen Ce, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Guangdong, established his authority, clarified discipline, and revised the regulations. Cultural achievement thereupon shone forth and flourished greatly. At that time, Ouyang Bijin, Supreme Commander and Grand Coordinator, holding the title of Right Vice Minister of War, directed civil affairs and invigorated military preparedness, securing and pacifying the southern territories. He reiterated his admonitions …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所司展采錯事先是巡按御
史黃如桂敷敭
德意表勵令甲無不豫所建張廼
禮聘宗和暨敎諭黃玉藻考
試敎諭張汝楠林服休江文
弼程伯鎬張緘同考試旣至
則右布政使蔡雲程左參政
===
沈應龍提調僉事張煌江以
朝監試而御史陳策寔監臨
之於是進提學副使蔡克廉
所簡士二千五百有奇三試
之得人七十有五以其名氏
及文之優者錄書以
獻宗和謹敘諸首竊謂今日所掄
punctuated: 所司展采錯事。先是，巡按御史黃如桂敷敭德意，表勵令甲，無不豫所建張。廼禮聘宗和暨敎諭黃玉藻考試，敎諭張汝楠、林服休、江文弼、程伯鎬、張緘同考試。旣至，則右布政使蔡雲程、左參政沈應龍提調，僉事張煌、江以朝監試，而御史陳策寔監臨之。於是進提學副使蔡克廉所簡士二千五百有奇，三試之，得人七十有五。以其名氏及文之優者錄書以獻，宗和謹敘諸首。竊謂今日所掄
translation_en:
…the responsible offices to discharge their duties and carry out their tasks. Before this, Regional Inspector Huang Rugui had proclaimed the imperial intentions and upheld and promoted the established regulations, making all necessary arrangements beforehand [?]. Zonghe and Instructor Huang Yuzao were then formally invited to serve as Examiners, and Instructors Zhang Runan, Lin Fuxiu, Jiang Wenbi, Cheng Bogao, and Zhang Jian as Associate Examiners. Once they arrived, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Cai Yuncheng and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Shen Yinglong served as Proctors; Surveillance Commissioners Zhang Huang and Jiang Yichao supervised the examination; and Censor Chen Ce served as its Supervising Official.
More than 2,500 candidates selected by Education Intendant Cai Kelian, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were then admitted. After three examination sessions, seventy-five men were selected. Their names and the best of their compositions were compiled into a volume for presentation to the throne, and I, Zonghe, respectfully composed this preface to place at its beginning. I venture to suggest that those selected today…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
固豫養之學校而教治於鄉
之吏者也其爲教也其鄉三
物者乎禮賓之制則無不合
乎成周而試之以文亦於德
行道藝有攷而賢者能者興
乎嘗伏讀
聖諭蓋拳拳曰崇正學迪正道夫
===
正學者堯舜禹湯文武周公
孔子之學也正道者堯舜禹
湯文武周公孔子之道也以
此得之爲六德以此行之爲
六行以此游之爲六藝而文
在其中矣初不謂立教作人
者孜孜誦書綴文以應有司
punctuated:
固豫養之學校，而教治於鄉之吏者也。其爲教也，其鄉三物者乎？禮賓之制，則無不合乎成周；而試之以文，亦於德行道藝有攷，而賢者能者興乎。嘗伏讀聖諭，蓋拳拳曰：「崇正學，迪正道。」
夫正學者，堯舜禹湯文武周公孔子之學也；正道者，堯舜禹湯文武周公孔子之道也。以此得之爲六德，以此行之爲六行，以此游之爲六藝，而文在其中矣。初不謂立教作人者，孜孜誦書綴文以應有司
translation_en:
…were indeed nurtured beforehand in the schools and instructed and governed by the officials of their local communities. As for this instruction, was it not instruction in the three categories of local education? The institutions for ceremonially honoring guests all accord with those of the Zhou dynasty in its flourishing age. Examining candidates through their writing likewise provides a means of assessing virtue, conduct, the Way, and the arts, so that the worthy and capable may be advanced. I once reverently read the imperial admonition, which earnestly declared: “Honor orthodox learning; follow the correct Way.”
Orthodox learning is the learning of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius. The correct Way is the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius. What one acquires through this constitutes the six virtues; what one puts into practice through this constitutes the six forms of conduct; what one cultivates through this constitutes the six arts. Literary accomplishment is included within these. It was never intended that those who establish instruction and cultivate talent should assiduously recite books and compose writings to satisfy the responsible officials …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之求而已夫不以誦書綴文
應有司爲立敎作人之務而
至有司之求卒不越乎書義
文詞之間何也道德者深縕
而未著也行藝者散見而易
飾也文則見之外而縕於中
可章著不可矯飾者也故曰
===
有德者有言蓋因言而知德
非貴彼之能言爾辟之借鑑
以別媸妍四方人士之林妍
媸淑慝之鏡舍文其奚以哉
又古者士初見必執質愼始
也今介質禮衰而文章人人
負以自信繇一介之臣脫跡
punctuated:
之求而已。夫不以誦書綴文應有司爲立敎作人之務，而至有司之求，卒不越乎書義文詞之間，何也？道德者，深縕而未著也；行藝者，散見而易飾也；文則見之外而縕於中，可章著、不可矯飾者也。故曰：「有德者有言。」蓋因言而知德，非貴彼之能言爾。辟之借鑑以別媸妍，四方人士之林，妍媸淑慝之鏡，舍文其奚以哉？
又古者士初見必執質，愼始也。今介質禮衰，而文章人人負以自信，繇一介之臣脫跡
translation_en:
…to meet the demands of the responsible officials, and nothing more. Now, if reciting books and composing prose to satisfy those officials is not the purpose of establishing instruction and cultivating men, why do the officials’ demands ultimately remain confined to interpretations of the classics and literary composition? The Way and virtue lie deeply stored within and are not yet manifest; conduct and accomplishments appear in scattered instances and are easily embellished. Writing, however, appears outwardly while holding its substance within: it can be made manifest, but cannot be counterfeited. Thus it is said: “Those who possess virtue have something to say.” It is through their words that we recognize their virtue; we do not prize merely their ability to speak. This is like borrowing a mirror to distinguish ugliness from beauty. Among the multitude of scholars from all quarters, what other mirror than writing could distinguish beauty from ugliness, goodness from wickedness?
Moreover, in antiquity, a scholar making his first formal visit invariably bore a presentation gift, taking care over the beginning of the relationship. Today, the rites of introduction and presentation gifts have declined, yet everyone relies on his literary compositions as grounds for confidence in himself. For a man who, from the position of a humble subject, emerges …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
草萊觀光
上國設不以文何爲利見之資
故錄名氏又錄文詞亦明有
質云爾當今
聖天子馭寓禮樂神化參賛兩儀
而道藝徳行之敎風行嶺海
蓋超然堯舜禹湯文武矣諸
===
士漸漬衣被爭相磨濯雲從
景附陳力宣猷當爲皐夔稷
契之臣無負周公孔子之道
詩曰王國克生維周之楨濟
濟多士文王以寧則斯錄也
固多士進身之信質
國家得賢之明鑑也如或不然
punctuated: 草萊，觀光上國，設不以文，何爲利見之資？故錄名氏，又錄文詞，亦明有質云爾。當今聖天子馭寓，禮樂神化，參賛兩儀，而道藝徳行之敎風行嶺海，蓋超然堯舜禹湯文武矣。諸士漸漬衣被，爭相磨濯，雲從景附，陳力宣猷，當爲皐夔稷契之臣，無負周公孔子之道。《詩》曰：「王國克生，維周之楨。」「濟濟多士，文王以寧。」則斯錄也，固多士進身之信質，國家得賢之明鑑也。如或不然，
translation_en: …from rustic obscurity to behold the splendor of the imperial capital: without literary composition, what would furnish the means for gaining a favorable audience? Thus we record their names and also their writings, simply to make clear that they, too, have gifts of introduction to present. Today our sagely Son of Heaven rules the realm [?]; through rites, music, and wondrous transformation, he assists Heaven and Earth in their work. Instruction in the Way, the arts, virtue, and conduct spreads like the wind throughout Linghai, surely attaining the lofty heights of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, and Kings Wen and Wu. Immersed in this influence and covered by its beneficence, the scholars vie to polish and cleanse themselves, following like clouds and adhering like shadows. Offering their abilities and carrying forward the sovereign’s plans, they should become ministers like Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie, and not fail the Way of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. The Book of Odes says: “The royal kingdom can bring forth men who are the pillars of Zhou”; and, “Numerous are the worthy scholars; through them King Wen enjoys peace.” This examination record is therefore both a trustworthy credential by which these scholars may advance and a clear mirror through which the state may find worthy men. If, however, this should not be so, …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
虛質耳其於斯鑑不有遜形
乎哉夫質而虛者不誠之過
鑑而遜者不明之招語云繇
忠信而後有禮忠信者誠也
諸士先立乎其誠宗和等不
明之罪吾知其免夫是舉也
提督都御史喻智兼振德威
丕揚風教總兵平江伯陳圭
雅崇儒術俎豆臨戎會瓊黎
不靖副使黃光昇錢嶸朱道
瀾右參議方民悅僉事徐緝
都指揮張國威各有事於兵
僉事陳崇慶參將馮文焯都
指揮俞大猷亦備兵它郡而
punctuated:
虛質耳，其於斯鑑不有遜形乎哉？夫質而虛者，不誠之過；鑑而遜者，不明之招。語云：「繇忠信而後有禮。」忠信者，誠也。諸士先立乎其誠，宗和等不明之罪，吾知其免。
夫是舉也，提督都御史喻智兼振德威，丕揚風教；總兵平江伯陳圭雅崇儒術，俎豆臨戎。會瓊黎不靖，副使黃光昇、錢嶸、朱道瀾，右參議方民悅，僉事徐緝，都指揮張國威，各有事於兵。僉事陳崇慶、參將馮文焯、都指揮俞大猷亦備兵它郡，而
translation_en:
…it would be merely an empty credential. Would they not shrink in shame from their own reflection in this mirror? An empty credential results from a failure of sincerity; shrinking before the mirror results from a failure of discernment. As the saying goes, “Only through loyalty and trustworthiness does ritual propriety become possible.” Loyalty and trustworthiness are sincerity. If the gentlemen first establish themselves in sincerity, I know that Zonghe and his colleagues will escape the charge of lacking discernment.
For this examination, Yu Zhi, Censor-in-chief serving as Military Superintendent, exercised both moral influence and authority, greatly promoting moral instruction. Chen Gui, Earl of Pingjiang and Regional Commander, had long esteemed Confucian learning and maintained ritual observances even amid military affairs. It happened that the Li people of Qiong were in unrest. Surveillance Vice Commissioners Huang Guangsheng, Qian Rong, and Zhu Daolan; Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Fang Minyue; Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Ji; and Regional Military Commissioner Zhang Guowei were each occupied with military matters. Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Chen Chongqing, Assistant Regional Commander Feng Wenzhuo, and Regional Military Commissioner Yu Dayou were likewise attending to military defenses in other prefectures, and…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
綜理要束文院以外惟左叅
議姜儀云左布政使韓楷以
考績行右叅政陳仕賢都指
揮劉滋以入
賀行按察使李遂副使朱憲章
左叅議項喬僉事張臬以遷
代去然竝與有襄翼者也書
===
之
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學
正林宗和謹序
punctuated:
綜理要束，文院以外，惟左叅議姜儀云。左布政使韓楷以考績行，右叅政陳仕賢、都指揮劉滋以入賀行，按察使李遂、副使朱憲章、左叅議項喬、僉事張臬以遷代去，然竝與有襄翼者也，書之。
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正林宗和謹序。
translation_en:
…outside the examination compound, only Jiang Yi, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner, remained to oversee the essential arrangements. Han Kai, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, departed for his performance evaluation. Chen Shixian, Right Administration Vice Commissioner, and Liu Zi, Regional Military Commissioner, departed to offer congratulations at court. Li Sui, Surveillance Commissioner; Zhu Xianzhang, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Xiang Qiao, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; and Zhang Nie, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, left upon transfer or replacement. Nevertheless, all contributed assistance, and I record them here.
This preface is respectfully composed by Lin Zonghe, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史陳策〔時偕福建莆田縣人乙未進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使蔡雲程〔亨之浙江臨海縣人己丑進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政沈應龍〔翔卿浙江烏程縣人乙未進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事張煌〔用韜福建閩縣人戊戌進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事江以朝〔于春江西貴溪縣人丙戌進士〕
===
考試官
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正林宗和〔節之福建晉江縣人癸卯貢士〕
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭黃玉藻〔仲冕福建莆田縣人庚子貢士〕
同考試官
福建汀州府長汀縣儒學教諭張汝楠〔伯材廣西桂林中衛籍臨桂縣人甲午貢士〕
直隸常州府武進縣儒學教諭林服休〔叔諧福建候官縣人癸卯貢士〕
湖廣永州府東安縣儒學教諭江文弼〔右卿貴州普定衛籍四川巴縣人丙午貢士〕
直隸池州府青陽縣儒學教諭程伯鎬〔朝京福建閩縣人癸卯貢士〕
江西南安府南康縣儒學教諭張緎〔時鳴湖廣湘鄉縣人癸卯貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按廣東監察御史陳策〔時偕，福建莆田縣人，乙未進士〕。

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使蔡雲程〔亨之，浙江臨海縣人，己丑進士〕。
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政沈應龍〔翔卿，浙江烏程縣人，乙未進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事張煌〔用韜，福建閩縣人，戊戌進士〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事江以朝〔于春，江西貴溪縣人，丙戌進士〕。

考試官：
河南汝寧府信陽州儒學學正林宗和〔節之，福建晉江縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭黃玉藻〔仲冕，福建莆田縣人，庚子貢士〕。

同考試官：
福建汀州府長汀縣儒學教諭張汝楠〔伯材，廣西桂林中衛籍，臨桂縣人，甲午貢士〕。
直隸常州府武進縣儒學教諭林服休〔叔諧，福建候官縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
湖廣永州府東安縣儒學教諭江文弼〔右卿，貴州普定衛籍，四川巴縣人，丙午貢士〕。
直隸池州府青陽縣儒學教諭程伯鎬〔朝京，福建閩縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
江西南安府南康縣儒學教諭張緎〔時鳴，湖廣湘鄉縣人，癸卯貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination of the Twenty-eighth Year of Jiajing (1549).

Supervising Official
Chen Ce, courtesy name Shixie, Regional Inspector of Guangdong and Investigating Censor, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the yiwei year.

Proctors
Cai Yuncheng, courtesy name Hengzhi, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong, was a native of Linhai County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.
Shen Yinglong, courtesy name Xiangqing, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, was a native of Wucheng County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Zhang Huang, courtesy name Yongtao, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, was a native of Min County, Fujian, and a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Jiang Yichao, courtesy name Yuchun, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Guangdong, was a native of Guixi County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Examiners
Lin Zonghe, courtesy name Jiezhi, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a native of Jinjiang County, Fujian, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the guimao year.
Huang Yuzao, courtesy name Zhongmian, Instructor at the Confucian School of Wan'an County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute student of the gengzi year.

Associate Examiners
Zhang Runan, courtesy name Bocai, was Instructor at the Confucian School of Changting County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian. He was registered with the Guilin Central Guard in Guangxi, was a native of Lingui County, and was a tribute student of the jiawu year.
Lin Fuxiu, courtesy name Shuxie, Instructor at the Confucian School of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a native of Houguan County, Fujian, and a tribute student of the guimao year.
Jiang Wenbi, courtesy name Youqing, was Instructor at the Confucian School of Dong'an County, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang. He was registered with the Puding Guard in Guizhou, was a native of Ba County, Sichuan, and was a tribute student of the bingwu year.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
君子學道則愛人
或生而知之或學而知之或困而知之及
其知之一也或安而行之或利而行之
或勉强而行之及其成功一也
其爲氣也至大至剛以直養而無害則塞
于天地之間其爲氣也配義與道無是
餒也
===
易
天行健君子以自彊不息
天地感而萬物化生聖人感人心而天下
和平觀其所感而天地萬物之情可見
矣
乾知大始坤作成物乾以易知坤以簡能
君子知微知彰知柔知剛萬夫之望
書
乃聖乃神乃武乃文
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
君子學道則愛人。
或生而知之，或學而知之，或困而知之，及其知之，一也。或安而行之，或利而行之，或勉强而行之，及其成功，一也。
其爲氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。其爲氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。

易
天行健，君子以自彊不息。
天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天下和平。觀其所感，而天地萬物之情可見矣。
乾知大始，坤作成物。乾以易知，坤以簡能。
君子知微知彰，知柔知剛，萬夫之望。

書
乃聖乃神，乃武乃文。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
When the gentleman studies the Way, he loves others.
Some know it from birth; some know it through study; some know it through struggling with difficulties. Once they know it, their knowledge is the same. Some practice it with ease; some practice it for its benefits; some practice it through strenuous effort. Once they achieve success, the result is the same.
As a vital force, it is supremely great and supremely firm. If nourished with uprightness and left unharmed, it fills the space between Heaven and Earth. As a vital force, it accords with righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves.

Book of Changes
Heaven moves with vigor; the gentleman accordingly strives unceasingly to strengthen himself.
Heaven and Earth influence one another, and the myriad things are transformed and brought into being. The sage moves human hearts, and all under Heaven is harmonious and at peace. By observing what they influence, one can discern the true nature of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things.
Qian governs the great beginning; Kun brings things to completion. Qian governs through ease; Kun accomplishes through simplicity.
The gentleman understands the subtle and the manifest, the yielding and the firm; he is the one to whom all people look.

Book of Documents
Sagacious and wondrous, martial and cultured.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其爾克紹乃辟于先王永綏民說拜稽首
曰敢對揚天子之休命
汝則從龜從筮從卿士從庶民從是之謂
大同身其康彊子孫其逢吉
爾克敬典在德時乃罔不變允升于大猷
詩
四月秀葽五月鳴蜩八月其穫十月隕蘀
民之質矣日用飲食羣黎百姓徧為爾德
虎拜稽首天子萬年
===
受小球大球為下國綴旒何天之休不競
不絿不剛不柔敷政優優百祿是遒受
小共大共為下國駿厖何天之龍敷奏
其勇不震不動不戁不竦百祿是總
春秋
蔡侯鄭伯會于鄧桓公二年
九月晉人執季孫行父舍之于苕丘十
有二月乙丑季孫行父及晉郤犨盟于
扈俱成公十有六年
punctuated:
其爾克紹乃辟于先王，永綏民。說拜稽首，曰：「敢對揚天子之休命。」
汝則從，龜從，筮從，卿士從，庶民從，是之謂大同。身其康彊，子孫其逢吉。
爾克敬典在德，時乃罔不變，允升于大猷。

詩
四月秀葽，五月鳴蜩。八月其穫，十月隕蘀。
民之質矣，日用飲食。羣黎百姓，徧為爾德。
虎拜稽首，天子萬年。
受小球大球，為下國綴旒，何天之休。不競不絿，不剛不柔，敷政優優，百祿是遒。受小共大共，為下國駿厖，何天之龍。敷奏其勇，不震不動，不戁不竦，百祿是總。

春秋
蔡侯、鄭伯會于鄧。桓公二年。
九月，晉人執季孫行父，舍之于苕丘。十有二月乙丑，季孫行父及晉郤犨盟于扈。俱成公十有六年。
translation_en:
…May you enable your sovereign to continue the work of the former kings and bring lasting peace to the people. Yue bowed and touched his forehead to the ground, saying: “I venture to acknowledge and extol the Son of Heaven’s gracious command.”

When you yourself concur, the tortoise-shell divination concurs, the milfoil divination concurs, the ministers concur, and the common people concur, this is called the Great Accord. You will enjoy health and strength, and your descendants will encounter good fortune.

If you can reverently observe the constant norms and attend to virtue, then none will fail to be transformed, and you will truly advance along the great Way.

Book of Odes

In the fourth month the yao plants flower; in the fifth month the cicadas sing. In the eighth month comes the harvest; in the tenth month the leaves fall.

The people’s basic needs are their daily food and drink. The multitudes, the hundred families, everywhere follow your virtue.

Hu bowed and touched his forehead to the ground: “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years!”

He receives small and large jade tokens and serves as the rallying point of the states below, bearing Heaven’s blessings. Neither contentious nor impetuous, neither hard nor soft, he administers government with generous ease, and all blessings gather about him. He receives small and great offerings and serves as a mighty support for the states below, bearing Heaven’s favor. He displays and puts forth his valor, neither shaken nor unsettled, neither fearful nor alarmed, and all blessings converge upon him.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Marquis of Cai and the Earl of Zheng met at Deng. Second year of Duke Huan.

In the ninth month, the men of Jin seized Jisun Xingfu and lodged him at Tiaoqiu. In the twelfth month, on the yichou day, Jisun Xingfu and Xi Chou of Jin made a covenant at Hu. Both entries are from the sixteenth year of Duke Cheng.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十
有二月己亥同盟于戲襄公九年公會
晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子齊世子
光滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭戍鄭
虎牢楚公子貞帥師救鄭俱襄公十年
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭
秋七月己未同盟于亳城北楚子鄭
===
伯伐宋公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊
世子光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子伐鄭會于蕭魚俱襄公十有一年
滕子來朝桓公二年齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰
田定公十年
禮記
是以君子恭敬撙節退讓以明禮
趨以采齊行以肆夏周還中規折還中矩
進則揖之退則揚之然後玉鏘鳴也
punctuated:
冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲。襄公九年。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，戍鄭虎牢。楚公子貞帥師救鄭。俱襄公十年。
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。秋七月己未，同盟于亳城北。楚子、鄭伯伐宋。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。俱襄公十有一年。
滕子來朝。桓公二年。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。定公十年。
禮記
是以君子恭敬撙節退讓以明禮。
趨以采齊，行以肆夏，周還中規，折還中矩。進則揖之，退則揚之，然後玉鏘鳴也。
translation_en:
In winter, the Duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, the Viscount of Little Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. On the jihai day of the twelfth month, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xi. Ninth year of Duke Xiang.
The Duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju and Zhu, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu in attacking Zheng. They garrisoned Hulao in Zheng. Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to relieve Zheng. Both passages are from the tenth year of Duke Xiang.
The Duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu in attacking Zheng. In autumn, on the jiwei day of the seventh month, they jointly concluded a covenant north of Bocheng. The Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng attacked Song. The Duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. All these passages are from the eleventh year of Duke Xiang.
The Viscount of Teng came to pay court. Second year of Duke Huan. Men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. Tenth year of Duke Ding.
Record of Rites
Thus the gentleman displays reverence, exercises restraint, and yields modestly, thereby making ritual propriety manifest.
When moving briskly, he keeps time to Gathering Shepherd’s Purse (Cai Qi); when walking, to Summer (Si Xia). His circling turns conform to the compass, and his angular turns conform to the carpenter’s square. When advancing, he inclines his body; when withdrawing, he raises it upright. Only then do his jade pendants chime.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄

所以感之者故禮以道其志樂以和其
聲政以一其行刑以防其姦禮樂刑政

年

六者非性也，感於物而后動。是故先王慎所以感之者。故禮以道其志，樂以和其聲，政以一其行，刑以防其姦。禮樂刑政，其極一也，所以同民心而出治道也。
故可以為文，可以為武，可以擯相，可以治軍旅。
第貳塲
論
聖人，人倫之至。
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢令郡國舉孝廉各一人詔，元光元年。
擬唐以房玄齡、杜如晦為僕射誥，貞觀三年。

translation_en:
These six are not inherent nature; they become active only when stirred by external things. Thus the former kings were careful about what stirred them. Ritual guides their aspirations; music harmonizes their voices; government unifies their conduct; punishments guard against their wrongdoing. Ritual, music, punishments, and government have one ultimate purpose: to unite the people's hearts and bring forth the way of good governance.
Thus one can perform civil duties, undertake military duties, assist at ceremonies, and command armies.
Second Session
Discourse
“The sage is the perfection of human relationships.”
One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han, ordering each commandery and kingdom to recommend one person distinguished for filial piety and integrity: first year of Yuanguang [134 BCE].
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang, appointing Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui as Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs: third year of Zhenguan [629].
Compose a memorial in the voice of Sima Guang of the Song, submitting a method for recommending men of talent under ten categories: first year of Yuanyou [1086].
Five Legal Judgments
Officials exceeding the time limit for proceeding to their posts.
Households to be determined according to the registers.
Offering sacrifices to deities included in the sacrificial canon.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
軍民約會詞訟
脩理橋梁道路
第叁塲
策〔五道〕
問書稱典則詩詠舊章所以經世範俗使
之畫一可守而施措有法見於載籍者
無國無典章焉考於今而周禮一書與
唐之六典其事猶著有足徵者恭惟我
太祖高皇帝立國垂統布令成法有綱有紀
===
列聖丕承潤色雖政歸法
祖而制與時宜蓋寢明寢備矣然皆未暇稽粹
定為一書迨于
敬皇而後會典始成不知其與周官唐典亦有
所取合否歟其所宗本以何書為主其
所纂輯於何書為据事無細而不錄厥
有何意令有寢而必書厥指安在今之
頒布服習其亦乆矣可得而頌言歟肆我
皇上邁德中興議禮制度光於
punctuated:
軍民約會詞訟。
脩理橋梁道路。

第叁塲
策〔五道〕

問：書稱典則，詩詠舊章，所以經世範俗，使之畫一可守，而施措有法。見於載籍者，無國無典章焉。考於今，而周禮一書與唐之六典，其事猶著，有足徵者。恭惟我太祖高皇帝立國垂統，布令成法，有綱有紀；列聖丕承潤色，雖政歸法祖，而制與時宜，蓋寢明寢備矣。然皆未暇稽粹，定為一書。迨于敬皇，而後會典始成。不知其與周官、唐典，亦有所取合否歟？其所宗本，以何書為主？其所纂輯，於何書為据？事無細而不錄，厥有何意？令有寢而必書，厥指安在？今之頒布服習，其亦乆矣，可得而頌言歟？肆我皇上邁德中興，議禮制度，光於
translation_en:
Lawsuits involving arrangements for military personnel and civilians to appear jointly [?].
Repairing bridges and roads.

Third Session
Policy Questions 〔Five questions〕

Question: The Book of Documents speaks of established standards, and the Book of Odes celebrates ancient statutes. These serve to order the world and regulate customs, making them uniform and capable of observance, and providing rules for administrative action. Among the states recorded in historical writings, none lacked institutions and statutes. Examining what survives today, we find that the Rites of Zhou and the Six Statutes of the Tang still preserve clear accounts of such matters and provide evidence sufficient for verification.

We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the state and established its succession, promulgated commands and instituted laws, providing both guiding principles and orderly regulations. The successive sage emperors carried forward and refined this great inheritance. Although government rested on following the ancestors, institutions were adapted to the needs of the times, becoming progressively clearer and more complete. Yet none had leisure to examine and assemble their essentials into a single book. Only under Emperor Jing was the Collected Statutes finally completed.

We wonder whether it drew upon, or accorded with, the Offices of Zhou and the statutes of the Tang. Which book was its principal foundation? Which books supplied the source material for its compilation? No matter was too small to record: what was the intention behind this? Even commands that had been suspended were invariably recorded: what was the purpose of this? It has now long been promulgated, studied, and put into practice. Can you set forth its merits?

Now our Sovereign, through surpassing virtue, has brought about a dynastic resurgence, deliberating on rites and establishing institutions, bringing glory to …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
列祖思弘永業以垂
後裔於是申
命儒臣特加脩輯將備所未備精而益精者也
孔子曰如或知爾則何以哉假令諸生
獲與載筆之列於是役也又何以佐於
下風
問樂本於聲律也尚矣昔人謂聲生於日
律生於辰其說可得聞歟夫聲有五固
矣其後有增二變而謂之七聲者昉於
===
===
疇歟又有謂七始七華者同歟否歟夫
三音俱不變而宮徵獨變者何歟律有
十二固矣其後有衍而相生爲六十律
者昉於疇歟又有爲十二均十一均者
同歟否歟夫聲律旋相爲宮而黃鍾獨
不爲他律役者又何歟夫曰正聲矣而
又曰子聲曰正律矣而又曰變律豈作
樂者必待於半變而後成歟魏晉以來
制樂律者多矣荀勉梁武之笛律何爲
punctuated:
列祖，思弘永業，以垂後裔。於是申命儒臣，特加脩輯，將備所未備，精而益精者也。孔子曰：「如或知爾，則何以哉？」假令諸生獲與載筆之列，於是役也，又何以佐於下風？
問：樂本於聲律也，尚矣。昔人謂聲生於日，律生於辰，其說可得聞歟？夫聲有五，固矣。其後有增二變而謂之七聲者，昉於疇歟？又有謂七始、七華者，同歟否歟？夫三音俱不變，而宮徵獨變者，何歟？律有十二，固矣。其後有衍而相生爲六十律者，昉於疇歟？又有爲十二均、十一均者，同歟否歟？夫聲律旋相爲宮，而黃鍾獨不爲他律役者，又何歟？夫曰正聲矣，而又曰子聲；曰正律矣，而又曰變律。豈作樂者必待於半變而後成歟？魏晉以來，制樂律者多矣。荀勉、梁武之笛律，何爲
translation_en:
…the successive imperial ancestors, and seeks to extend his enduring enterprise so that it may be handed down to his descendants. He therefore renewed his command to the Confucian officials to undertake a special revision and compilation, intending to supply what was still lacking and to refine it still further. Confucius said: “If someone were to recognize your abilities, what would you do?” Supposing that you candidates were given a place among those entrusted with the writing, how would you assist in a subordinate capacity in this undertaking?
Question: Music has been based on tones and pitch standards since antiquity. People of old said that tones arise from the days and pitch standards from the earthly branches marking time. May we hear an explanation of this theory? That there are five tones is established. Who first added the two altered tones, thus making what are called the seven tones? There are also what are called the “seven beginnings” and “seven blossoms” [?]: are these the same or not? Why do the other three tones remain unaltered, while gong and zhi alone have altered forms? That there are twelve pitch standards is established. Who first extended them through successive generation to produce sixty pitch standards? There are also systems of twelve and eleven tonal frameworks (jun): are these the same or not? Since the tones and pitch standards take turns serving as gong, why is Huangzhong alone not made to serve the other pitch standards? We speak of principal tones, yet also of subsidiary tones; we speak of regular pitch standards, yet also of altered pitch standards. Must the making of music await these half-pitches and alterations before it can be complete? Since the Wei and Jin dynasties, many have established musical pitch standards. The flute pitch standards of Xun Mian [?] and Emperor Wu of Liang—why …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不同杜夔阮咸之校尺何爲互異夫律
定於尺尺成於黍何世之論者紛紛於
短長廣狹之辨而莫之一也諸士講究
有年將必有妙解神悟如師曠州鳩者
願敷言之以爲
今日虞廷作樂之助
問古者六藝之文射其一也制則成周大
具有射人以掌射法而司常司裘樂師
司馬太僕太史中書各有所職以治其
===
事其名則大射賓射燕射之分而六弓
八矢及夫射侯射耦射地射節之異等
威品節較森然也要之義何居至其敎
士則以鄉射不知所以爲敎者又何如
也周衰禮廢漢唐之君間舉以行之我
國家置圃學宮輯定射儀
頒天下章明悉備莫可尚已然置射於學果
卽鄉射之敎而射儀所載亦於成周之
制有同異乎否也夫禮觀會通時因損
punctuated:
不同？杜夔、阮咸之校尺何爲互異？夫律定於尺，尺成於黍，何世之論者紛紛於短長廣狹之辨，而莫之一也？諸士講究有年，將必有妙解神悟如師曠、州鳩者，願敷言之，以爲今日虞廷作樂之助。
問：古者六藝之文，射其一也。制則成周大具，有射人以掌射法，而司常、司裘、樂師、司馬、太僕、太史、中書各有所職，以治其事。其名則大射、賓射、燕射之分，而六弓八矢及夫射侯、射耦、射地、射節之異，等威品節，較森然也。要之，義何居？至其敎士，則以鄉射，不知所以爲敎者又何如也？周衰禮廢，漢唐之君間舉以行之。我國家置圃學宮，輯定射儀，頒天下，章明悉備，莫可尚已。然置射於學，果卽鄉射之敎，而射儀所載，亦於成周之制有同異乎否也？夫禮觀會通，時因損
translation_en:
…differ? Why did Du Kui and Ruan Xian arrive at different results when checking the measuring rule? Pitch standards are determined by the measuring rule, and the rule is established from millet grains. Why have scholars through the ages disputed its length and breadth without reaching agreement? You gentlemen have studied these matters for years and surely possess subtle understanding and inspired insight like Shi Kuang and Zhou Jiu. Please expound your views, thereby assisting the creation of music at today’s court of Shun.
Question: Archery was one of the six arts of antiquity. Its institutions became fully developed under the Zhou. There was a Director of Archery to oversee its methods, while the Director of Banners, Director of Fur Robes, Music Master, Minister of War, Grand Coachman, Grand Scribe, and Palace Secretary [?] each had assigned duties in managing its affairs. Its named forms were the Great Archery Ceremony, Guest Archery, and Banquet Archery. There were six kinds of bows and eight kinds of arrows, as well as distinctions in targets, paired contestants, shooting grounds, and rhythmic measures for shooting. The gradations of rank and dignity and the prescribed ceremonial forms were clearly and rigorously ordered. What, in essence, was their significance? As for instructing scholars, this was done through District Archery. How, then, did it serve to instruct them? As the Zhou declined, its rites fell into disuse; rulers of the Han and Tang occasionally revived and practiced them. Our dynasty has established archery grounds at schools, compiled and fixed the archery ceremonies, and promulgated them throughout the realm. These regulations are clear and comprehensive, unsurpassed in their completeness. Yet does establishing archery in schools truly embody the instruction provided by District Archery? And do the provisions of the archery ceremonies agree with, or differ from, the institutions of the Zhou? In considering ritual, one examines how its provisions connect and apply across circumstances, adapting them to the times through reductions …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
益諸生漸濡
聖化歌且習於斯吾知其不待敎而興者然化
裁通變之宜神明鼓舞之用其尚有道
乎
問氏族所以尊祖敬宗序世系明昭穆其
從來遠矣今試舉一二商之稽古有以
國氏者有以地氏者有以字以名氏者
又有以次以族以官氏者其義云何有
以凶德氏者有以吉德氏者有以技以
===
事氏者又有以族系氏以謚氏以爵氏
者其指安在至於以志爲氏以美之字
爲氏以所封之邑爲氏以一時之事爲
氏又率意而更其姓者有之豈果可以
巳爲之歟甚者氏以聲近而訛以字近
而訛族以姓多而訛以望多而訛又因
姓而妄附他人者有之豈又果無一定
歟紀氏族者有世家有譜局令史有譜
牒其能序别之否也論氏族者有風俗
punctuated:
益。諸生漸濡聖化，歌且習於斯，吾知其不待敎而興者。然化裁通變之宜，神明鼓舞之用，其尚有道乎？

問：氏族所以尊祖敬宗，序世系，明昭穆，其從來遠矣。今試舉一二，商之稽古。有以國氏者，有以地氏者，有以字以名氏者，又有以次以族以官氏者，其義云何？有以凶德氏者，有以吉德氏者，有以技以事氏者，又有以族系氏、以謚氏、以爵氏者，其指安在？至於以志爲氏，以美之字爲氏，以所封之邑爲氏，以一時之事爲氏，又率意而更其姓者有之，豈果可以巳爲之歟？甚者，氏以聲近而訛，以字近而訛；族以姓多而訛，以望多而訛；又因姓而妄附他人者有之，豈又果無一定歟？紀氏族者有世家，有譜局令史，有譜牒，其能序别之否也？論氏族者有《風俗》
translation_en:
…and additions. You students have been steeped in the sage emperor’s transforming influence, singing and practicing here; I know that you will be inspired without waiting for instruction. Yet is there a way to adapt and modify these practices appropriately as circumstances change, and to exercise that spiritually discerning power which rouses and inspires?

Question: Clans and surnames serve to honor ancestors and respect the ancestral line, arrange genealogical succession, and clarify the alternating generational positions of zhao and mu. Their origins are ancient indeed. Let us now take a few examples and examine them against antiquity. Some took their clan names from states, some from places, some from courtesy names or personal names, and others from birth order, kin groups, or offices. What principles underlie these practices? Some took clan names from evil qualities, others from good qualities, and others from skills or activities; still others took them from lineage affiliations, posthumous names, or noble ranks. What was the significance of these choices? There were also those who took clan names from their aspirations, from characters with favorable meanings, from towns granted to them as fiefs, or from particular events; and some changed their surnames at whim. Could they really do this on their own authority [?]? Worse still, clan names became corrupted through similarities in sound or written form, and clan affiliations became confused through the multiplicity of surnames or of prestigious ancestral seats. Some even used a shared surname to attach themselves falsely to other people’s lineages. Could there really be no fixed standard?

Among those recording clans and surnames were accounts of hereditary houses, clerks of genealogical bureaus, and genealogical registers. Were they able to arrange and distinguish these affiliations? Among works discussing clans and surnames, there is Customs …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
通有元和姓纂有宰相表其能釐正之
否也夫不得與於德宗之譜者乃傳致
其訛不能齒於城南之牒者乃鑿摘其
失甚哉氏族之不可不講也茲欲定譜
牒如成周小史所職使天下曉然不紊
於宗祖是非以成棠棣行葦之美其道
何繇也爾諸生抱博古務本之學其必
有能詳之者願毋泛毋略
問瓊海文物彬然甚盛也然而環黎為居
咫尺有夷夏之辨夫黎固人類耳絃歌
聲聞不可一入其心豈性與人殊哉而
威信法約亦嘗有土舍以領制之者也
生黎誠愚熟黎不聞大將之號令乎而
今乃數數不靖至廑
上命赫然舉兵將誅之夫以萬全之力視此直
狐鼠耳其束身繫頸可計日待也然欲
為久安長輯之計其道何繇兵家所談
要不越乎撫守戰三者書生之論將不
punctuated:
通，有《元和姓纂》，有《宰相表》，其能釐正之否也？夫不得與於德宗之譜者，乃傳致其訛；不能齒於城南之牒者，乃鑿摘其失。甚哉，氏族之不可不講也！茲欲定譜牒，如成周小史所職，使天下曉然不紊於宗祖是非，以成《棠棣》《行葦》之美，其道何繇也？爾諸生抱博古務本之學，其必有能詳之者，願毋泛毋略。

問：瓊海文物彬然甚盛也，然而環黎為居，咫尺有夷夏之辨。夫黎固人類耳，絃歌聲聞不可一入其心，豈性與人殊哉？而威信法約，亦嘗有土舍以領制之者也。生黎誠愚，熟黎不聞大將之號令乎？而今乃數數不靖，至廑上命，赫然舉兵將誅之。夫以萬全之力視此，直狐鼠耳，其束身繫頸，可計日待也。然欲為久安長輯之計，其道何繇？兵家所談，要不越乎撫、守、戰三者，書生之論將不
translation_en:
…Comprehensive Discussions of Customs, the Yuanhe Compilation of Surnames, and the Tables of Chief Ministers: can these rectify the errors? Those who could not gain inclusion in Dezong’s genealogy went on to transmit its errors [?]; those who could not be ranked in the Chengnan genealogical register proceeded to pick out its faults through strained interpretations [?]. How essential it is to study clans and lineages! Now, if we wish to establish genealogical registers as was the responsibility of the Junior Historiographer under the Zhou, enabling everyone throughout the realm to distinguish clearly between correct and incorrect ancestral affiliations without confusion, and thereby realize the virtues celebrated in “The Cherry Tree” and “The Reeds,” by what means can this be accomplished? You students pursue learning that embraces antiquity and attends to fundamentals. Surely some among you can explain this fully. Please be neither vague nor cursory.

Question: Qionghai flourishes splendidly in culture and institutions. Yet its inhabitants dwell amid the Li, and within the shortest distance there is a distinction between the uncivilized and the civilized. The Li are, after all, human beings. If the sounds of strings and song cannot enter their hearts at all, can it be that their nature differs from that of other people? As for authority, trust, laws, and covenants, there have also been native officials’ sons (tushe) appointed to lead and control them. The unassimilated Li may indeed be ignorant, but have the assimilated Li not heard the commanding general’s orders? Yet now they repeatedly cause unrest, to the point of troubling His Majesty to issue a command, wrathfully dispatching troops to punish them. Viewed against our forces, whose success is assured, they are merely foxes and rats. We can count the days until they present themselves bound, with cords around their necks. But by what means can we devise a plan for enduring peace and lasting concord? What military specialists discuss comes down to three things: pacification, defense, and warfare. Will the discussions of scholars not…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
在是歟謂斯人之無不可化不知化黎
亦有其人乎諸生生長斯土請先陳華
心宣化之圖而后及於川原夷險之勢
叛服失得之因如何古者出兵受成於
學行將在泮獻馘也故以此質之諸生
punctuated: 在是歟？謂斯人之無不可化，不知化黎亦有其人乎？諸生生長斯土，請先陳華心宣化之圖，而后及於川原夷險之勢、叛服失得之因，如何？古者出兵，受成於學，行將在泮獻馘也，故以此質之諸生。
translation_en: …lie within these approaches as well? It is said that none of these people is beyond moral transformation; but are there also men capable of transforming the Li? You students were born and raised in this land. Please first set forth a plan for turning their hearts toward Chinese civilization [?] and spreading moral instruction, and then address the configuration of rivers and plains, the ease or difficulty of the terrain, and the causes of rebellion and submission, failure and success. How should these matters be handled? In antiquity, before troops were dispatched, settled plans were received at the school; soon the ears severed from slain enemies will be presented at the prefectural school. Thus we put these questions to you students.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子學道則愛人
胡庭蘭
同考試官敎諭江批治道以禮樂爲急禮樂
以養人爲本觀聖人答爲邦之問槩可見矣此作
中和明贍豈亦學道而有得者歟可以占其用矣
考試官敎諭黃批文有體貼故不易得也
考試官學正林批精當
===
君子而知所學則有仁者之施焉夫愛人仁之
施而學道斯知學也知所學則其施如此君子
可不學以爲務乎此夫子之言子游旣試於武
城者夫子哂之故以此對若曰偃之以禮樂爲
敎是非敢於自用也蓋嘗聞敎於夫子矣彼發
政宣令而治人者君子也其責治人其道不在
於責人也於是有君子之學焉學不知道猶弗
學也有志乎學是必有志乎道其視天下之道
皆吾性之所有也循其典常之則而豫立夫出
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
君子學道則愛人
胡庭蘭
同考試官敎諭江批：治道以禮樂爲急，禮樂以養人爲本。觀聖人答爲邦之問，槩可見矣。此作中和明贍，豈亦學道而有得者歟？可以占其用矣。
考試官敎諭黃批：文有體貼，故不易得也。
考試官學正林批：精當。
君子而知所學，則有仁者之施焉。夫愛人，仁之施；而學道，斯知學也。知所學，則其施如此，君子可不學以爲務乎？此夫子之言，子游旣試於武城者。夫子哂之，故以此對，若曰：偃之以禮樂爲敎，是非敢於自用也，蓋嘗聞敎於夫子矣。彼發政宣令而治人者，君子也。其責治人，其道不在於責人也。於是有君子之學焉。學不知道，猶弗學也。有志乎學，是必有志乎道。其視天下之道，皆吾性之所有也。循其典常之則，而豫立夫出
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When the gentleman studies the Way, he loves others”
Hu Tinglan

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: In the way of governing, rites and music are the most urgent concern; rites and music take nurturing people as their foundation. This can be seen in broad outline from the Sage’s answer to the question about governing a state. This composition is balanced and harmonious, lucid and ample. Might its author also be someone who has studied the Way and gained something from it? From this one may anticipate his usefulness in office.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The writing shows an intimate appreciation of its subject and is therefore no easy achievement.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Refined and apt.

When a gentleman knows what he should study, his actions express benevolence. Loving others is the expression of benevolence, while studying the Way is knowing how to learn. If knowing what to study leads to such actions, can the gentleman fail to make learning his principal concern? These were the Master’s words, which Ziyou had already put to the test at Wucheng. The Master smiled at him, so he replied with these words, as if to say: “In making rites and music the basis of instruction, I, Yan, have not presumed to act on my own judgment. Rather, I once received this teaching from you, Master.” Those who promulgate policies, issue commands, and govern others are gentlemen. Their responsibility is to govern others, but their way of doing so does not lie in making demands upon others. Hence there is the learning proper to a gentleman. To study without knowing the Way is as though one had not studied at all. Whoever aspires to learning must aspire to the Way. He regards all the principles of the world as inherent in his own nature. Following their enduring standards, he establishes beforehand the source from which to issue…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
政之原會其貞一之趨而精察夫使民之本則
凡禮以治躬樂以治心學之弗得弗措也如是
而愛人之體立矣吾見其身脩道其道不獨於
成身也於是有愛人之仁焉人本一體莫非我
也有見於道則必無見於我其視天下之人皆
斯道之所關也擴同胞之義而自切懷保之恩
推理一之公而尤廑匡翼之敎則凡升之大猷
錫之皇極一夫不獲予辜也如是而學道之用
行矣是非聞見之學也脩身以立敎而天理之
===
含蓄深厚而有餘亦非强勉之愛也體仁以長
人而生意之流行真切而莫遏故不患無仁人
之施而患淑已之道未至不患無博施之用而
患體道之學未充是則君子之道然也偃之敎
人禮樂正以敎人學道也道無分於君子小人
禮樂可以邑小而棄之耶噫偃之心其自許乎
愛人之心矣夫子之晒蓋喜之也抑小人學道
則聞絃歌其在武城然耳然非君子學道以先
之何以使民之知學耶故觀於小人所以敎武
punctuated:
政之原，會其貞一之趨，而精察夫使民之本，則凡禮以治躬、樂以治心，學之弗得弗措也。如是而愛人之體立矣。吾見其身脩道，其道不獨於成身也，於是有愛人之仁焉。人本一體，莫非我也。有見於道，則必無見於我。其視天下之人，皆斯道之所關也。擴同胞之義，而自切懷保之恩；推理一之公，而尤廑匡翼之敎。則凡升之大猷、錫之皇極，一夫不獲，予辜也。如是而學道之用行矣。是非聞見之學也，脩身以立敎，而天理之含蓄深厚而有餘；亦非强勉之愛也，體仁以長人，而生意之流行真切而莫遏。故不患無仁人之施，而患淑已之道未至；不患無博施之用，而患體道之學未充。是則君子之道然也。偃之敎人禮樂，正以敎人學道也。道無分於君子小人，禮樂可以邑小而棄之耶？

噫！偃之心，其自許乎愛人之心矣。夫子之晒，蓋喜之也。抑小人學道，則聞絃歌，其在武城然耳。然非君子學道以先之，何以使民之知學耶？故觀於小人，所以敎武
translation_en:
…the source of governance, comprehend its orientation toward constancy and unity, and closely examine the foundation of employing the people. Then, in all that concerns using ritual to govern one’s conduct and music to govern one’s heart, one will not cease studying until one has mastered them. In this way, the foundation for loving others is established. I see him personally cultivating the Way [?]; his Way does not stop at perfecting himself. From this arises the benevolence that loves others. Other people originally form one body with us: none is separate from oneself. Once one perceives the Way, one must cease to see oneself as separate. One regards all people under Heaven as bound up with this Way. By extending the principle that all are siblings, one makes the kindness of cherishing and protecting them one’s own urgent concern; by extending the impartiality of the single principle, one devotes particular care to teaching that corrects and supports them. Thus, in raising them to the great Way and bestowing upon them the sovereign standard, one holds that, if even a single person fails to find his proper place, “the fault is mine.” In this way, learning the Way becomes effective in practice.

This is no mere learning through hearing and seeing. One cultivates oneself to establish instruction, and the principle of Heaven is stored within, profound, substantial, and abundant. Nor is this a love forced through effort. One embodies benevolence to lead others, and the flow of life-giving vitality is genuine, earnest, and unstoppable. Thus one worries not about lacking a benevolent person’s beneficent deeds, but about failing to attain the Way of perfecting oneself; not about lacking the capacity to benefit others widely, but about incompleteness in the learning through which one embodies the Way. Such is the Way of the gentleman. Yan’s teaching people ritual and music was precisely his means of teaching them to learn the Way. The Way makes no distinction between gentlemen and common people. Could ritual and music be abandoned merely because a town is small?

Ah! Yan surely considered his own heart to be a heart that loved others. The Master’s smile was surely an expression of delight in him. Yet as for common people learning the Way, it was in Wucheng that the sound of stringed instruments and singing was heard. But unless a gentleman learned the Way and led them in doing so, how could the people be brought to understand learning? Thus, considered in relation to the common people, his means of teaching Wu…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
城旣至矣觀於君子其所學於洙泗者不亦深
歟
或生而知之或學而知之或困而知之及
其知之一也或安而行之或利而行之
或勉强而行之及其成功一也
金文業
同考試官教諭林批此題入手多率易而作
故往往令人厭觀是篇辭意精鍊而閑雅自如可
以式矣
===
考試官教諭黃批講畢餘意自長題之法
考試官學正林批簡明
聖人第言入道之等而要其歸之同也蓋道人
之所同具也入之有等者質之殊耳而謂其不
同歸也可乎夫子言此以道進哀公也意謂天
下之達道固以達德而行謂之德則無不同者
得乎天者也而賦於人有質焉謂之人於是乎
各一其質矣有生而知之者有學而知之者有
因而知之者生知者不思而得也學知者思而
punctuated:
城，旣至矣；觀於君子，其所學於洙泗者不亦深歟？
或生而知之，或學而知之，或困而知之，及其知之，一也；或安而行之，或利而行之，或勉强而行之，及其成功，一也。
金文業
同考試官教諭林批：此題入手多率易而作，故往往令人厭觀。是篇辭意精鍊，而閑雅自如，可以式矣。
考試官教諭黃批：講畢，餘意自長，題之法。
考試官學正林批：簡明。
聖人第言入道之等，而要其歸之同也。蓋道，人之所同具也；入之有等者，質之殊耳，而謂其不同歸也可乎？夫子言此，以道進哀公也。意謂天下之達道，固以達德而行。謂之德，則無不同者，得乎天者也。而賦於人，有質焉；謂之人，於是乎各一其質矣。有生而知之者，有學而知之者，有因而知之者。生知者，不思而得也；學知者，思而
translation_en:
…cheng, his teaching had already attained its fullest extent. Considering him as a gentleman, was not his learning by the Zhu and Si Rivers also profound?
“Some know it from birth; some know it through study; some know it through difficulty. Once they know it, their knowledge is one and the same. Some practice it with ease; some practice it for its benefit; some practice it through strenuous effort. Once they achieve success, their accomplishment is one and the same.”
Jin Wenye
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Writers commonly approach this topic carelessly, so their essays often weary the reader. This piece is refined in both expression and meaning, yet remains effortlessly composed and elegant. It can serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “When the exposition is complete, its further implications unfold of themselves: this is the method for treating the topic [?].”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Concise and clear.”
The Sage merely speaks of the different levels at which people enter the Way, while emphasizing that they ultimately arrive at the same destination. For the Way is something all people possess alike. That there are different levels of entry is simply due to differences in their native constitution. Can one therefore claim that they do not reach the same destination? The Master said this to advance Duke Ai in the Way. His meaning was that the universally applicable Way of the world is indeed practiced through the universally applicable virtues. As virtues, these are alike in everyone, for they are received from Heaven. Yet when they are endowed in human beings, there is a particular constitution; as human beings, each thus has a constitution of his own. Some know it from birth; some know it through study; some know it through dependence [?; the transcription reads 因, apparently for 困, “difficulty”]. Those who know it from birth apprehend it without reflection. Those who know it through study reflect and…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
后得也困知者思之不得困於其心而后作也
夫執此而高下之將曰聞道有蚤莫然而人患
不悟道耳蚤者有悟莫者亦有悟要皆明乎善
而已生知學知困知其知同其致同則謂之心
同可也而有異乎有安而行之者有利而行之
者有勉强而行之者安行者不習而利也利行
者習而后利也勉强者習而不利作之不止而
后成也夫視此而優劣之將曰行道有難易然
而人患不至道耳易者可至難者亦可至要皆
===
復其初而已安行利行勉行其行同其功同則
謂之道同可也而又有異乎始以德而同中以
質而異人之自雜其天也而終之所不異又原
於其始之同天之未離乎人也自雜其天而謂
身之不可入德賊其身者也未離乎人而謂人
之不可語道誣其人者也然則脩人以完天變
異而反之同吾人可不勉歟抑知道者知行道
者仁知之成功而一者勇三德之不可缺一也
然其知知此其行行此其一一此夫豈有二物
punctuated: 后得也。困知者，思之不得，困於其心而后作也。夫執此而高下之，將曰聞道有蚤莫。然而人患不悟道耳，蚤者有悟，莫者亦有悟，要皆明乎善而已。生知、學知、困知，其知同，其致同，則謂之心同可也，而有異乎？有安而行之者，有利而行之者，有勉强而行之者。安行者，不習而利也；利行者，習而后利也；勉强者，習而不利，作之不止而后成也。夫視此而優劣之，將曰行道有難易。然而人患不至道耳，易者可至，難者亦可至，要皆復其初而已。安行、利行、勉行，其行同，其功同，則謂之道同可也，而又有異乎？始以德而同，中以質而異，人之自雜其天也；而終之所不異，又原於其始之同，天之未離乎人也。自雜其天而謂身之不可入德，賊其身者也；未離乎人而謂人之不可語道，誣其人者也。然則脩人以完天，變異而反之同，吾人可不勉歟？抑知道者知，行道者仁，知之成功而一者勇，三德之不可缺一也。然其知知此，其行行此，其一一此，夫豈有二物
translation_en:
…and only afterward attain understanding. Those who come to know through difficulty think without attaining understanding; only after distress within their hearts do they rouse themselves to effort. If one uses these distinctions to rank people higher or lower, one will say that some hear the Way early and others late. Yet the real concern is simply that people fail to awaken to the Way. Those who come early awaken to it, and those who come late also awaken to it: ultimately, all alike understand goodness. Whether they know from birth, know through learning, or know through difficulty, their knowledge is the same and what they attain is the same. Thus one may say that their minds are the same. What difference is there?

Some practice it with natural ease, some practice it for its benefit, and some practice it through strenuous effort. Those who practice with natural ease do so smoothly without practice; those who practice for its benefit do so smoothly only after practice; those who exert themselves strenuously practice without ease, and succeed only after unceasing effort. If one uses these distinctions to judge people superior or inferior, one will say that practicing the Way is difficult for some and easy for others. Yet the real concern is simply that people fail to reach the Way. Those who find it easy can reach it, and those who find it difficult can also reach it: ultimately, all alike recover their original state. Whether they practice with ease, for benefit, or through effort, their practice is the same and their achievement is the same. Thus one may say that their Way is the same. What difference, then, is there?

At the beginning they are alike in virtue; along the way they differ in their endowments. This is because people themselves introduce admixture into what Heaven has bestowed upon them. Yet their eventual lack of difference is rooted in their original sameness: Heaven has never become separated from humanity. To introduce admixture into one’s Heaven-given nature oneself and then claim that one cannot enter into virtue is to injure oneself. Since Heaven has never become separated from humanity, to claim that a person cannot be spoken to about the Way is to misrepresent that person. Thus, by cultivating the human, we preserve the wholeness of the Heaven-given; by transforming our differences, we return to sameness. Can we fail to exert ourselves?

Moreover, knowing the Way is wisdom; practicing the Way is benevolence; and knowing it and bringing one’s achievement to the same fulfillment is courage. Not one of these three virtues can be lacking. Yet what their knowing knows is this, what their practice practices is this, and what their unity unifies is this. How could there be two separate things…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
哉故曰所以行之者一也君子於此又當求知
行合一之學
其為氣也至大至剛以直養而無害則塞
于天地之間其為氣也配義與道無是
餒也
謝良任
同考試官教諭張批氣塞天地須就人身言
始有發揮故又曰配道與義是作最得孟子之意
同考試官教諭程批氣壯辭昌子固負浩然
之氣者
===
考試官教諭黃批結引易大壯義甚發明
考試官學正林批文氣浩然
大賢論浩然之氣必著其本體而極其功用焉
蓋剛大而塞天地氣之本體也養之成焉則其
功用斯配乎道義矣善養之功其可已乎孟子
告公孫丑之意若曰浩然之氣固為難言而亦
有可以言者彼大而或可限非大之至也乃若
其氣則不離於形而不囿於形語大天下莫能
punctuated:
哉？故曰：「所以行之者一也。」君子於此又當求知行合一之學。

「其為氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。其為氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。」
謝良任

同考試官教諭張批：「氣塞天地，須就人身言，始有發揮。故又曰配道與義，是作最得孟子之意。」
同考試官教諭程批：「氣壯辭昌，子固負浩然之氣者。」

考試官教諭黃批：「結引《易》大壯，義甚發明。」
考試官學正林批：「文氣浩然。」

大賢論浩然之氣，必著其本體而極其功用焉。蓋剛大而塞天地，氣之本體也；養之成焉，則其功用斯配乎道義矣。善養之功，其可已乎？孟子告公孫丑之意若曰：浩然之氣固為難言，而亦有可以言者。彼大而或可限，非大之至也。乃若其氣，則不離於形而不囿於形，語大，天下莫能
translation_en:
…could there be two distinct things? Thus it is said: “That by which they are put into practice is one.” Here the gentleman should further pursue the learning that unites knowledge and action.

“As qi, it is supremely great and supremely firm. If nourished with uprightness and left unharmed, it fills the space between Heaven and Earth. As qi, it accords with righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves.”
Xie Liangren

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “To explain how qi fills Heaven and Earth, one must discuss it in relation to the human person; only then can its meaning be developed. Hence the further statement that it accords with the Way and righteousness. This essay captures Mencius’s meaning exceptionally well.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: “The vital force is vigorous and the language abundant. You indeed possess this vast, flowing qi.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The conclusion cites the Great Strength hexagram of the Book of Changes, bringing out its meaning very clearly.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The vital force of the writing is vast and flowing.”

When the great worthy discusses the vast, flowing qi, he necessarily reveals its fundamental nature and fully explores its efficacy. Firm and great, filling Heaven and Earth: such is the fundamental nature of qi. Once its nourishment has been brought to completion, its efficacy accords with the Way and righteousness. Can the work of nourishing it well ever cease? The purport of Mencius’s words to Gongsun Chou is as follows: Vast, flowing qi is indeed difficult to describe, yet there are things that can be said of it. Something that is great but can still be bounded is not great in the highest degree. This qi, however, neither departs from bodily form nor is confined by it. In speaking of its greatness, nothing under Heaven can …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
載焉不亦大之至乎剛而或可屈非剛之至也
乃若其氣則不外於體而不局於體語剛天下
莫能撓焉不亦剛之至乎人惟不能善養之爾
使能加存養之功優游以俟其自化不以私智
戕之則大者無失其為大而磅礴渾淪殆塞兩
間而無外矣務擴充之學紓徐以俟其自成弗
以人力參之則剛者無失其為剛而周流布濩
殆彌六合而無窮矣夫氣之為氣本如此則其
養成之功用何如哉蓋吾之氣即天地之正氣
===
也而實理以宰之吾之理即天地之正理也而
必氣以輔之今惟氣合于理則義乗氣以出所
以裁制萬事者若有以翼其能定大計决大疑
固强立而不反焉理合于氣則道附氣以行所
以綱維萬事者若有以賛其勇當大任臨大變
固獨往而不懼焉使無是氣則柔巽不能以自
振見義不為或失之無勇矣疑懼不能以自立
遵道而行必半塗而廢矣豈不至於餒耶夫氣
之繫於人其大如此信乎氣之不可以不養也
punctuated: 載焉，不亦大之至乎？剛而或可屈，非剛之至也。乃若其氣，則不外於體而不局於體，語剛，天下莫能撓焉，不亦剛之至乎？人惟不能善養之爾。使能加存養之功，優游以俟其自化，不以私智戕之，則大者無失其為大，而磅礴渾淪，殆塞兩間而無外矣。務擴充之學，紓徐以俟其自成，弗以人力參之，則剛者無失其為剛，而周流布濩，殆彌六合而無窮矣。夫氣之為氣本如此，則其養成之功用何如哉？蓋吾之氣即天地之正氣也，而實理以宰之；吾之理即天地之正理也，而必氣以輔之。今惟氣合于理，則義乗氣以出，所以裁制萬事者，若有以翼其能，定大計、决大疑，固强立而不反焉。理合于氣，則道附氣以行，所以綱維萬事者，若有以賛其勇，當大任、臨大變，固獨往而不懼焉。使無是氣，則柔巽不能以自振，見義不為，或失之無勇矣；疑懼不能以自立，遵道而行，必半塗而廢矣，豈不至於餒耶？夫氣之繫於人，其大如此，信乎氣之不可以不養也！
translation_en:
…contain it. Is this not greatness in its utmost degree? What is firm but can sometimes be bent is not firmness in its utmost degree. As for this qi, it is neither outside the body nor confined within it. Speaking of its firmness, nothing under Heaven can bend it: is this not firmness in its utmost degree? It is only that people fail to nourish it well. If one could devote effort to preserving and nourishing it, awaiting its spontaneous transformation with unhurried ease and not injuring it through self-serving cleverness, then what is great would retain its greatness. Vast and undivided, it would fill the space between Heaven and Earth, leaving nothing outside it. If one devoted oneself to the learning that extends and enlarges it, calmly awaiting its spontaneous completion without interfering through human effort, then what is firm would retain its firmness. Circulating everywhere and spreading throughout, it would pervade the six directions without limit. Since this is the inherent nature of qi, what, then, are its effective powers once its nourishment has been brought to completion?

Our qi is the correct qi of Heaven and Earth, and principle truly governs it; our principle is the correct principle of Heaven and Earth, and it necessarily requires qi to support it. When qi accords with principle, righteousness issues forth borne upon qi. That by which one judges and regulates all affairs seems to receive assistance to its capacity: in settling great plans and resolving great doubts, one assuredly stands firm without turning back. When principle accords with qi, the Way proceeds supported by qi. That by which one orders and sustains all affairs seems to receive aid to its courage: in undertaking great responsibilities and confronting great upheavals, one assuredly advances alone without fear. Without this qi, one would be weak and yielding, unable to rouse oneself; seeing what is right but failing to act, one might fall short through lack of courage. Doubtful and fearful, unable to stand on one's own, one would set out along the Way only to abandon it halfway. Would one not thus become depleted? Such is the immense significance of qi for human beings. Truly, qi must be nourished!

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考諸易曰大壯利貞象曰雷在天上大壯君子
以非禮弗履夫乾之剛也震之動也是固浩然
之氣也非禮之勝正大之利是直養無害塞天
地而配道義也正大見天地之情剛大參天地
之化善養之極也故知大易之大壯則知孟子
之浩然矣
易
天行健君子以自彊不息
崔吉
===
同考試官教諭張批自彊不息則與天行同
健君子憲天之學聖學也此作得旨宜錄之
同考試官教諭程批此題作者多分爲兩段
殊失本意此篇詞意渾融其殆深於易者
考試官教諭黃批心學意正如此
考試官學正林批明整
天道有不已之象君子有不已之學夫天惟至
健故其行不已也君子自彊而純亦不已斯爲
善法天者矣夫子大象之意蓋以三陽之卦爲
punctuated:
考諸《易》曰：「大壯，利貞。」《象》曰：「雷在天上，大壯；君子以非禮弗履。」夫乾之剛也，震之動也，是固浩然之氣也。非禮之勝，正大之利，是直養無害，塞天地而配道義也。正大見天地之情，剛大參天地之化，善養之極也。故知大易之大壯，則知孟子之浩然矣。

易
「天行健，君子以自彊不息。」
崔吉

同考試官教諭張批：「自彊不息，則與天行同健。君子憲天之學，聖學也。此作得旨，宜錄之。」
同考試官教諭程批：「此題作者多分爲兩段，殊失本意。此篇詞意渾融，其殆深於易者。」
考試官教諭黃批：「心學意正如此。」
考試官學正林批：「明整。」

天道有不已之象，君子有不已之學。夫天惟至健，故其行不已也。君子自彊而純亦不已，斯爲善法天者矣。夫子大象之意，蓋以三陽之卦爲
translation_en:
Examining this in the Book of Changes, we find: “Great Strength: perseverance is beneficial.” The Commentary on the Images says: “Thunder above Heaven: Great Strength. Thus the gentleman takes no step contrary to ritual propriety.” The firmness of Qian and the movement of Zhen are indeed the vast, flowing vital force. The overcoming of what is contrary to ritual propriety [?] and the benefit of rectitude and greatness constitute nourishing this force with uprightness without harming it, so that it fills Heaven and Earth and accords with the Way and righteousness. Rectitude and greatness reveal the true disposition of Heaven and Earth; firmness and greatness participate in their transforming activity. This is the highest attainment in properly nourishing the vital force. Thus, understanding Great Strength in the great Book of Changes enables one to understand Mencius’s vast, flowing vital force.

Book of Changes
“Heaven’s movement is vigorous; thus the gentleman strengthens himself without ceasing.”
Cui Ji

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “By strengthening himself without ceasing, one shares the vigor of Heaven’s movement. The gentleman’s learning, which takes Heaven as its model, is the learning of the sages. This composition grasps the essential meaning and should be included.”

Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “Most writers on this topic divide it into two sections, entirely missing its original meaning. In this essay, expression and meaning form an integrated whole. Its author probably has a profound understanding of the Book of Changes.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of the learning of the mind is precisely this.”

Examiner Lin, School Instructor, comments: “Clear and orderly.”

The Way of Heaven exhibits an image of ceaseless activity; the gentleman pursues ceaseless learning. It is because Heaven is supremely vigorous that its movement never ceases. When the gentleman strengthens himself and likewise remains unceasing in his purity, he may be said to model himself well on Heaven. The Master’s meaning in the Commentary on the Great Images is, presumably, to take the trigram of three yang lines as …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乾其象則天也上下皆乾是天之行也今日一
周明日又一周迭運有常一日之員機無暫停
也循環不窮萬古之順動未少變也非至健者
能之乎健以主不息之用行以達至健之體此
天之所爲天也天不息道之在人亦不息人而
操舍之相乘反覆之爲害於是違天遠矣謂君
子之法天也有是哉吾知至精以察天人之機
而一之以無慾無慾則剛也至健以致理欲之
決而守之以無妄無妄則誠也成性恒存而道
===
心爲主於內無使終食之違有事勿正而人心
退聽於外不容一息之懈其蘊也天之性也會
動靜於一原而無或二或三之雜其發也天之
情也合終始於一致而無日至月至之憂蓋惟
至剛也故常伸任天下之重而險夷不變者此
也惟至誠也故無息致天下之遠而悠久無疆
者此也非自彊何以不息非不息又何以自彊
此君子之所爲君子也天行健者天之乾自彊
不息者我之乾也天健而行不息於造化君子
punctuated: 乾，其象則天也。上下皆乾，是天之行也。今日一周，明日又一周，迭運有常，一日之員機無暫停也；循環不窮，萬古之順動未少變也。非至健者能之乎？健以主不息之用，行以達至健之體，此天之所爲天也。天不息，道之在人亦不息。人而操舍之相乘，反覆之爲害，於是違天遠矣。謂君子之法天也，有是哉？吾知至精以察天人之機，而一之以無慾，無慾則剛也；至健以致理欲之決，而守之以無妄，無妄則誠也。成性恒存，而道心爲主於內，無使終食之違；有事勿正，而人心退聽於外，不容一息之懈。其蘊也，天之性也，會動靜於一原，而無或二或三之雜；其發也，天之情也，合終始於一致，而無日至月至之憂。蓋惟至剛也，故常伸，任天下之重而險夷不變者，此也；惟至誠也，故無息，致天下之遠而悠久無疆者，此也。非自彊，何以不息？非不息，又何以自彊？此君子之所爲君子也。「天行健」者，天之乾；「自彊不息」者，我之乾也。天健而行，不息於造化；君子
translation_en: …Qian; its image is Heaven. With Qian both above and below, this represents Heaven’s movement. Today it completes one circuit; tomorrow it completes another. Its successive revolutions follow a constant course: the revolving mechanism [?] does not pause for a moment throughout the day. Its cycles are inexhaustible: through all antiquity its orderly movement has never altered in the slightest. Could anything other than utmost vigor accomplish this? Vigor governs its unceasing operation, and movement gives expression to the substance of utmost vigor. This is what makes Heaven Heaven. Heaven does not cease; neither does the Way within human beings. Yet when holding fast and letting go alternate, and vacillation does harm, people depart far from Heaven. Could such conduct be called the gentleman’s emulation of Heaven? I understand that one must employ the utmost refinement to discern the workings of Heaven and humanity, unifying them through freedom from desire; freedom from desire brings firmness. One must employ utmost vigor to bring the distinction between principle and desire to a decisive resolution, preserving it through freedom from falsity; freedom from falsity brings sincerity. Keep one’s fully realized nature constantly present, so that the moral mind rules within, never departing from it even for the duration of a meal. Remain engaged in cultivation without anticipating results, so that the human mind withdraws and submits without, allowing not a single breath’s slackening. What is stored within is Heaven’s nature: activity and stillness are united in one source, without the admixture of divided or shifting purposes. What issues forth is Heaven’s feeling: beginning and end are joined in consistency, without the concern that one might attain it only for a day or a month. It is precisely because of utmost firmness that one constantly presses forward: this enables one to bear the weightiest responsibilities under Heaven without changing amid danger or ease. It is precisely because of utmost sincerity that one never ceases: this enables one to reach the farthest bounds under Heaven and endure without limit. Without strengthening oneself, how could one be unceasing? Without being unceasing, how could one strengthen oneself? This is what makes the gentleman a gentleman. “Heaven’s movement is vigorous” describes Heaven’s Qian; “strengthening oneself without ceasing” describes the Qian within oneself. Heaven moves with vigor, unceasing in its creative transformations; the gentleman…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
疆而行天健於一身人而配天然則君子旣聖
矣乎抑是君子也其孰以之中庸曰文王之德
之純是已然行曰天行在天無心也彊曰自疆
於人無力也天無心故健力不由人故不息吾
人爲不用力耳一日用其力未有力不足者然
其可以有心彊致之哉曰勿忘勿助得之
乾知大始坤作成物乾以易知坤以簡能
同考試官教諭張批發明乾坤生成易簡非
===
體認之深者不能及此佳士佳士
同考試官教諭程批詞氣明暢而精密無冗
贅語非衆作可及
考試官教諭黃批典雅可式
考試官學正林批簡潔
大傳卽乾坤相須之功而表其德焉夫知始作
成功則相須也於此不有見其易簡之德乎此
言乾坤之理分見於天地也若曰乾道成男坤
道成女若乾坤之各專其一矣然相對者固相
punctuated:
疆而行天健於一身，人而配天。然則君子旣聖矣乎？抑是君子也，其孰以之？《中庸》曰：「文王之德之純。」是已。然行曰天行，在天無心也；彊曰自疆，於人無力也。天無心故健，力不由人故不息。吾人爲不用力耳，一日用其力，未有力不足者。然其可以有心彊致之哉？曰：「勿忘勿助。」得之。
乾知大始，坤作成物。乾以易知，坤以簡能。
同考試官教諭張批：發明乾坤生成易簡，非體認之深者不能及此。佳士！佳士！
同考試官教諭程批：詞氣明暢而精密，無冗贅語，非衆作可及。
考試官教諭黃批：典雅可式。
考試官學正林批：簡潔。
《大傳》卽乾坤相須之功而表其德焉。夫知始作成，功則相須也，於此不有見其易簡之德乎？此言乾坤之理分見於天地也。若曰：「乾道成男，坤道成女。」若乾坤之各專其一矣。然相對者固相
translation_en:
…is strong and enacts Heaven’s vigor in his own person, matching Heaven while remaining human. Does this mean that the gentleman is already a sage? Yet who can attain to being such a gentleman [?]? The Doctrine of the Mean says, “The purity of King Wen’s virtue.” This is precisely it. Yet when movement is called Heaven’s movement, Heaven acts without deliberate intent; when strength is called self-strengthening, in the human being it involves no exertion. Heaven is vigorous because it has no deliberate intent; because the strength does not derive from human effort, it never ceases. It is simply that we do not exert ourselves. Once we exert our strength, it has never proved insufficient. Yet can this be forcibly attained through deliberate intent? The saying “Neither forget it nor help it along” captures the meaning.
Qian presides over the great beginning; Kun brings things to completion. Qian presides through ease; Kun accomplishes through simplicity.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: This elucidates the ease and simplicity with which Qian and Kun generate and complete things. Only someone with a deep personal understanding could reach this level. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!
Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: The language and tenor are lucid and fluent, yet precise and closely reasoned, without redundant or superfluous wording. Ordinary compositions cannot equal it.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: Classically elegant and worthy of serving as a model.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Concise and clear.
The Great Commentary reveals the virtues of Qian and Kun through their mutually dependent achievements. In presiding over beginnings and bringing things to completion, their achievements depend upon each other. Do we not see here their virtues of ease and simplicity? This speaks of the principles of Qian and Kun as manifested respectively in Heaven and Earth. As for the saying, “The way of Qian makes the male; the way of Kun makes the female,” it seems as though Qian and Kun each exclusively governs one category. Yet those that stand opposite each other indeed mutually…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
因以全其用並立者實並運以効其功以言乎
乾乾之所主先天下之化而不獨於男也一氣
先之肇其根一理先之命其性蓋即一物而無
所不始合萬物而無所不知其知大始乎曰始
則機緘猶微而未顯矣以言乎坤坤之所爲后
天下之化而不獨於女也性命於此而各正太
和於此而保合蓋承天施而無所不成舉物類
而無所不作其作成物乎曰作則形迹已著而
可求矣夫知物之始若甚難矣而乾至健其德
===
行恒易化機一動而遂通生意隨感而俱得物
物而始之匪物物而命之其始可言也其知不
可言也其知之妙乎使其不易何以大其知耶
作物之成若甚煩矣而坤至順其德行恒簡因
天之有以資生代終之外無他事物物而成之
匪物物而雕之其成可見也其作不可見也其
能之妙乎使其不簡何以廣其能耶要之始物
者乾所以始者乾無與也成物者坤所以成者
坤無與也易知者無知也易能者無能也故曰
punctuated: 因以全其用，並立者實並運以効其功。以言乎乾，乾之所主，先天下之化，而不獨於男也。一氣先之，肇其根；一理先之，命其性。蓋即一物而無所不始，合萬物而無所不知，其知大始乎！曰始，則機緘猶微而未顯矣。以言乎坤，坤之所爲，后天下之化，而不獨於女也。性命於此而各正，太和於此而保合。蓋承天施而無所不成，舉物類而無所不作，其作成物乎！曰作，則形迹已著而可求矣。夫知物之始，若甚難矣，而乾至健，其德行恒易。化機一動而遂通，生意隨感而俱得。物物而始之，匪物物而命之。其始可言也，其知不可言也。其知之妙乎！使其不易，何以大其知耶？作物之成，若甚煩矣，而坤至順，其德行恒簡。因天之有以資生，代終之外無他事。物物而成之，匪物物而雕之。其成可見也，其作不可見也。其能之妙乎！使其不簡，何以廣其能耶？要之，始物者乾，所以始者乾無與也；成物者坤，所以成者坤無與也。易知者無知也，易能者無能也。故曰：
translation_en:
…depend upon one another to fulfill their functions; those that stand alongside one another in fact operate together to accomplish their work. Speaking of Qian, the Creative: what Qian governs precedes the transformations of all under Heaven and is not confined to the male. The single vital force goes before them, establishing their roots; the single principle goes before them, conferring their natures. Thus, taking any one thing, there is nothing in it that Qian does not initiate; taking the myriad things together, there is nothing that Qian does not govern through knowing. Is this not its knowing the great beginning? To speak of a beginning is to say that the workings are still subtle and have not yet become manifest. Speaking of Kun, the Receptive: what Kun does follows the transformations of all under Heaven and is not confined to the female. Through it, each thing’s nature and allotted destiny are set right, and supreme harmony is preserved in union. Thus, receiving Heaven’s bestowal, it leaves nothing incomplete; among all the kinds of things, there is none that it does not bring into being. Is this not its making things complete? To speak of making is to say that forms and traces have already become manifest and can be investigated.

To know the beginnings of things might seem exceedingly difficult, yet Qian is supremely vigorous, and the exercise of its virtue is always easy. Once the impulse of transformation stirs, it flows freely; the intent to generate life is realized in every response. Qian initiates each and every thing, yet does not issue commands to each individually. Its initiating can be described, but its knowing cannot be described. How wondrous is its knowing! Were it not easy, how could it make its knowing great? To bring things to completion might seem exceedingly troublesome, yet Kun is supremely compliant, and the exercise of its virtue is always simple. Drawing upon what Heaven provides to sustain generation, it has no task beyond bringing things to completion on Heaven’s behalf. Kun completes each and every thing, yet does not carve each individually. Its completion can be seen, but its making cannot be seen. How wondrous is its capacity! Were it not simple, how could it extend its capacity broadly?

In essence, it is Qian that initiates things, yet Qian does not intervene in that by which they are initiated; it is Kun that completes things, yet Kun does not intervene in that by which they are completed. Knowing through ease is knowing without deliberate knowing; capacity through ease [?] is capacity without deliberate exertion of capacity. Thus it is said: …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
無心而成化至矣哉嗚呼易而易知人之良知
也簡而易從人之良能也法乾之易不在乎乾
法坤之簡不在乎坤曰在我而已
書
乃聖乃神乃武乃文
吳壽齡
同考試官教諭林批此作以天地鬼神雷霆
日月推廣題意甚切聖神文武之德且渾厚老成
讀之宛然見聖人氣象宜錄以式
===
考試官教諭黃批善發聖人之蘊
考試官學正林批明快高古
大臣賛聖帝之德有不可測之妙焉甚矣聖德
之盛也聖神文武隨所變而見焉耳夫孰得而
測之乎此伯益所以賛堯者也蓋曰德淪于有
象者每易於形容而妙入于無方者殆難以窺
識帝之德惟其廣而運也則其變化之妙何如
耶吾見其睿通乎微不待思慮之勞大入于化
無俟學習之力猶夫天地之大渾然而無迹也
punctuated:
無心而成化，至矣哉！嗚呼！易而易知，人之良知也；簡而易從，人之良能也。法乾之易，不在乎乾；法坤之簡，不在乎坤。曰在我而已。
書
乃聖乃神乃武乃文
吳壽齡
同考試官教諭林批：此作以天地、鬼神、雷霆、日月推廣題意，甚切聖神文武之德，且渾厚老成。讀之，宛然見聖人氣象，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭黃批：善發聖人之蘊。
考試官學正林批：明快高古。
大臣賛聖帝之德，有不可測之妙焉。甚矣，聖德之盛也！聖神文武，隨所變而見焉耳，夫孰得而測之乎？此伯益所以賛堯者也。蓋曰：德淪于有象者，每易於形容；而妙入于無方者，殆難以窺識。帝之德，惟其廣而運也，則其變化之妙何如耶？吾見其睿通乎微，不待思慮之勞；大入于化，無俟學習之力。猶夫天地之大，渾然而無迹也。
translation_en:
…To accomplish transformation without deliberate intent—how consummate! Ah! Being easy and thus readily known is humanity’s innate knowledge; being simple and thus readily followed is humanity’s innate capacity. To emulate Qian’s ease does not depend on Qian; to emulate Kun’s simplicity does not depend on Kun. It lies, I say, in oneself alone.

Book of Documents
“Sagely and numinous, martial and cultured”
Wu Shouling

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: This composition develops the meaning of the topic through Heaven and Earth, ghosts and spirits, thunder, and the sun and moon. It closely accords with the virtues of sageliness, numinousness, culture, and martial prowess, and is substantial and mature. Reading it, one seems to behold the bearing of a sage. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: It skillfully brings out the sage’s inner riches.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Lucid and vigorous, lofty and antique.

A great minister, praising the virtue of the sage emperor, finds in it a subtlety beyond fathoming. How abundant is sagely virtue! Sageliness, numinousness, culture, and martial prowess appear according to its changing manifestations; who could fathom it? This is why Bo Yi praised Yao. His meaning was this: virtue immersed in perceptible forms is generally easy to describe, but that whose subtlety enters the realm without fixed bounds is surely difficult to discern. Since the emperor’s virtue is vast and active, what must be the subtlety of its transformations? I see his sagely intelligence penetrating the imperceptible without the labor of deliberation, his greatness entering the realm of transformation without awaiting the effort of study and practice. It is like the vastness of Heaven and Earth, an undivided whole leaving no trace…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則既謂之聖矣而又見其神焉知來者研其幾
而不得其朕也妙應者藏諸用而莫識其端也
運而無方圓而不滯蓋有與鬼神同其幽者矣
夫曰聖曰神自可見言之也見其聖而謂之聖
見其神而謂之神帝固不知也夫豈可以易擬
耶不但是也吾見其以無私為威自有以畏天
下之志以不殺為勇自無以容天下之姦猶夫
雷霆之威凜然不可犯也則既謂之武矣而又
見其文焉和順積而英華發炳蔚以成其章也
===
博厚極而高明著經緯以盡其變也抑而愈揚
遏而愈光蓋有與日月合其明者矣夫曰武曰
文自所變言之也變以武而名之武變以文而
名之文帝固無心也夫豈可以輕測耶夫帝德
之妙如此此所以能盡克艱之實也舜也欲盡
其道當於帝之德而效法焉可矣舜聖德也言
克艱而必歸之堯不自聖之心也然後知舜之
讓也而為服善之虛益之賛也而為效忠之勤
師師諤諤之風固有並行而不悖者矣虞廷之
punctuated: 則既謂之聖矣，而又見其神焉。知來者研其幾而不得其朕也，妙應者藏諸用而莫識其端也。運而無方，圓而不滯，蓋有與鬼神同其幽者矣。夫曰聖曰神，自可見言之也。見其聖而謂之聖，見其神而謂之神，帝固不知也，夫豈可以易擬耶？不但是也，吾見其以無私為威，自有以畏天下之志；以不殺為勇，自無以容天下之姦。猶夫雷霆之威，凜然不可犯也。則既謂之武矣，而又見其文焉。和順積而英華發，炳蔚以成其章也；博厚極而高明著，經緯以盡其變也。抑而愈揚，遏而愈光，蓋有與日月合其明者矣。夫曰武曰文，自所變言之也。變以武而名之武，變以文而名之文，帝固無心也，夫豈可以輕測耶？夫帝德之妙如此，此所以能盡克艱之實也。舜也欲盡其道，當於帝之德而效法焉可矣。舜聖德也，言克艱而必歸之堯，不自聖之心也。然後知舜之讓也，而為服善之虛；益之賛也，而為效忠之勤。師師諤諤之風，固有並行而不悖者矣。虞廷之
translation_en:
…Thus, having called him sagely, we also perceive his spiritual efficacy. In his knowledge of what is to come, one may investigate its incipient signs yet find no trace of it; his wondrous responsiveness lies hidden in its operation, and none can discern its beginnings. It moves without fixed form, turns freely without obstruction, and shares the inscrutable depth of ghosts and spirits. To speak of him as sagely or spiritually efficacious is to speak from what can be perceived. Seeing his sageliness, we call him sagely; seeing his spiritual efficacy, we call him spiritually efficacious. The emperor himself is unaware of this. How could he readily be appraised? Nor is this all. I see that he makes impartiality his majesty, thereby awing the hearts of all under Heaven; he makes refraining from killing his courage, yet leaves no room for the wickedness of all under Heaven. Like the might of thunder, he inspires awe and cannot be affronted. Thus, having called him martial, we also perceive his civil refinement. Harmony and compliance accumulate within, and their splendid flowering emerges, radiant and luxuriant, forming a patterned beauty. His breadth and depth reach their utmost, and his loftiness and brilliance become manifest; like warp and weft, they encompass every transformation. The more he is pressed down, the higher he rises; the more he is checked, the brighter he shines. His radiance indeed matches that of the sun and moon. To speak of him as martial or civil is to speak of the forms his transformations take. When these manifest the martial, we call him martial; when they manifest the civil, we call him civil. The emperor himself has no deliberate intention in this. How could he lightly be fathomed?

Such is the wondrous character of the emperor’s virtue. This is why he could fully realize what it means to take the difficulties of rulership seriously. If Shun wished to fulfill this Way, he had only to take the emperor’s virtue as his model. Shun himself possessed sagely virtue, yet whenever he spoke of taking difficulties seriously, he invariably credited Yao: this expressed a heart that did not regard itself as sagely. Only then do we understand that Shun’s deference expressed the humility of submitting to goodness, while Yi’s praise expressed diligence in rendering loyal service. The practices of learning from one another and speaking with unflinching candor could indeed proceed together without conflict. The governance of the court of Yu…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
治益隆有以哉
爾克敬典在德時乃罔不變允升于大猷
陳德純
同考試官敎諭林批題本平易作者非涉腐
贅則務奇僻是篇詞不襲而理獨優讀之風味自
別也錄之
考試官敎諭黃批發敬典在德意親切
考試官學正林批理致氣格不羣佳士
賢王於大臣責以躬行之實而期以化成之效
===
焉夫實德足以感人也躬行以率之則民化於
道也自有不容已矣成王欲君陳弘訓而示以
端本之治也若曰治不本於身者治之末也化
不至於道者化之淺也是故倡導有本而應感
有機為君陳者當知尚矣彼典者吾之常道也
不可忽也德者吾之實理也不可僞也爾能持
寅畏之心而察帝則以左右兢兢乎惟恐其或
墜焉秉欽翼之念而奉天理以周旋惴惴乎惟
惧其或失焉不惟敬於心而且體於身深造以
punctuated:
治益隆，有以哉！
「爾克敬典在德，時乃罔不變，允升于大猷。」
陳德純
同考試官敎諭林批：「題本平易，作者非涉腐贅，則務奇僻。是篇詞不襲而理獨優，讀之風味自別也。錄之。」
考試官敎諭黃批：「發敬典在德意親切。」
考試官學正林批：「理致氣格不羣，佳士。」
賢王於大臣，責以躬行之實，而期以化成之效焉。夫實德足以感人也，躬行以率之，則民化於道也，自有不容已矣。成王欲君陳弘訓，而示以端本之治也。若曰：「治不本於身者，治之末也；化不至於道者，化之淺也。是故倡導有本，而應感有機，為君陳者當知尚矣。彼典者，吾之常道也，不可忽也；德者，吾之實理也，不可僞也。爾能持寅畏之心，而察帝則以左右，兢兢乎惟恐其或墜焉；秉欽翼之念，而奉天理以周旋，惴惴乎惟惧其或失焉。不惟敬於心，而且體於身，深造以
translation_en:
…there was indeed a reason why the government of Shun’s court grew ever more flourishing!

“If you can reverently observe the constant norms, grounding yourself in virtue, then none will fail to change, and they will truly advance to the Great Way.”

Chen Dechun

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The topic is fundamentally straightforward. Writers either lapse into stale verbosity or strive for the bizarre and obscure. This essay’s language is free from imitation, and its reasoning is outstanding. Reading it, one finds a distinctive savor. Selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “It brings out precisely and aptly the meaning of ‘reverently observing the constant norms, grounding oneself in virtue.’”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Its reasoning, spirit, and style are exceptional. A fine scholar.”

A worthy king demands from his great ministers the substance of personal practice and expects from them the results of fully realized moral transformation. Genuine virtue is sufficient to move others. When one leads them through personal practice, the people’s transformation in accordance with the Way naturally becomes irresistible. King Cheng wished Jun Chen to spread his instructions and showed him how to govern by rectifying the foundation. It was as though he said:

“Government that does not take one’s own person as its foundation attends only to the branches of government; transformation that does not bring people to the Way is shallow transformation. Thus, leadership has its foundation, and the response it evokes has its activating source. You, Jun Chen, should know what to esteem. These constant norms are our enduring Way and must not be neglected. Virtue is the principle genuinely embodied within us and must not be counterfeited. If you can maintain a heart of reverent awe and scrutinize the Supreme Lord’s standards in all your actions, remain vigilant, fearing only that you might let them fall away. Hold fast to reverence and watchfulness, and uphold Heaven’s principle in all your dealings, remaining apprehensive, fearing only that you might lose it. Not only revere it in your heart, but also embody it in your person, advancing deeply by means of…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
道之下自得夫居安資深之機而匪由於襲取
者矣不惟措之躬而且得之心率履不越之餘
眞足爲軌世範俗之本而不待於强爲者矣夫
如是則爾之所得者實而其所好者誠矣吾見
誠之動物不令而行而昔之百姓不親者莫不
去其物欲之累實之感人不疾而速而向之五
品不遜者悉皆革其習染之汙敏于其德也遷
于其善也藹然成禮義之俗而相忘於皇極之
天信乎治道日進于休明而否者於是爲泰矣
===
敦于其倫也若于其性也蔚然成文物之邦而
率由於王道之盛信乎世運日臻于熈皞而汙
者於是爲隆矣是何也典者所共由者也以此
而導之故民之入也易德者所固有者也以此
而率之故民之感也深所謂從厥攸好者此也
不然命且違之矣吁必如此而後可以弘周公
之訓抑自古之民必從其好堯舜帥天下以仁
而民從之從所好也然殷民之頑以武王服之
周公毖之其仁至矣而尚不從乃成王猶致望
punctuated: 道之下，自得夫居安資深之機，而匪由於襲取者矣。不惟措之躬，而且得之心，率履不越之餘，眞足爲軌世範俗之本，而不待於强爲者矣。夫如是，則爾之所得者實，而其所好者誠矣。吾見誠之動物，不令而行，而昔之百姓不親者，莫不去其物欲之累；實之感人，不疾而速，而向之五品不遜者，悉皆革其習染之汙。敏于其德也，遷于其善也，藹然成禮義之俗，而相忘於皇極之天。信乎治道日進于休明，而否者於是爲泰矣。敦于其倫也，若于其性也，蔚然成文物之邦，而率由於王道之盛。信乎世運日臻于熈皞，而汙者於是爲隆矣。是何也？典者，所共由者也，以此而導之，故民之入也易；德者，所固有者也，以此而率之，故民之感也深。所謂從厥攸好者，此也。不然，命且違之矣。吁！必如此而後可以弘周公之訓。抑自古之民必從其好，堯舜帥天下以仁，而民從之，從所好也。然殷民之頑，以武王服之，周公毖之，其仁至矣，而尚不從，乃成王猶致望
translation_en:
…through the Way, you will naturally attain the means to dwell securely in it and draw deeply upon it, without merely borrowing from others. You will not only put it into practice in your person but also grasp it in your heart. Through following the proper course without transgression, you will truly possess a foundation for setting standards for the world and models for its customs, without having to force your conduct. In this way, what you have attained will be substantial, and what you cherish will be sincere.

I see that sincerity moves others: without orders, they act, and those among the common people who formerly lacked affection for one another will all cast off the burden of their material desires. Genuine substance touches people: without haste, its effects are swift, and those who formerly failed to observe the five human relationships will all cleanse themselves of the defilement of ingrained habits. They will strive diligently in virtue and advance toward goodness. Customs of ritual propriety and righteousness will flourish, and people will live together without self-conscious effort beneath the heaven of the august ultimate standard. Truly, the way of government will advance daily toward excellence and enlightenment, and obstruction will thereby turn into harmonious prosperity. They will strengthen their human relationships and accord with their inherent nature. Their land will flourish in cultural refinement, and all will follow the flourishing Kingly Way. Truly, the fortunes of the age will daily attain greater brightness and harmony, and decline will thereby give way to ascendancy.

Why is this so? Constant norms are what all alike follow. Guide the people by these, and they will readily enter the proper path. Virtue is what they inherently possess. Lead them by it, and they will be deeply moved. This is what is meant by their following what their ruler cherishes. Otherwise, they will disobey even his commands. Ah! Only by acting thus can you extend the Duke of Zhou’s teachings.

Yet from antiquity the people have always followed what their rulers cherish. Yao and Shun led all under Heaven through benevolence, and the people followed them: they followed what their rulers cherished. But as for the obstinate people of Yin, King Wu subdued them, and the Duke of Zhou exercised vigilance over them. Their benevolence was consummate, yet these people still would not follow. Nevertheless, King Cheng still placed his hopes…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于君陳何耶蓋堯舜承時雍之世武周當變革
之時勢不同耳故出治者貴端本論治者貴識
勢
詩
虎拜稽首天子萬年
同考試官教諭江批作此題者語病陳俗是
篇清新精切令人誦讀不厭且忠愛之意溢於言
外高薦何疑
===
考試官教諭黃批理明辭鬯非苟作者
考試官學正林批得祝壽意
大臣之於君也致敬以受命而祝壽以答恩焉
夫感恩思報臣下之義也大臣敬於受命而答
恩則稱壽焉其忠愛何至哉昔宣王命召穆公
平淮夷詩人美之及此若曰君之使臣也有勸
功之典臣之愛君也有報德之誠召虎於王何
如哉彼王念江漢之功也蕃錫寵臨彰榮世美
其策命可謂隆矣虎也蒙自天之恩澤而俯拜
punctuated:
于君陳，何耶？蓋堯舜承時雍之世，武周當變革之時，勢不同耳。故出治者貴端本，論治者貴識勢。

詩
虎拜稽首，天子萬年。

同考試官教諭江批：作此題者，語病陳俗。是篇清新精切，令人誦讀不厭，且忠愛之意溢於言外，高薦何疑？

考試官教諭黃批：理明辭鬯，非苟作者。

考試官學正林批：得祝壽意。

大臣之於君也，致敬以受命，而祝壽以答恩焉。夫感恩思報，臣下之義也。大臣敬於受命，而答恩則稱壽焉，其忠愛何至哉！昔宣王命召穆公平淮夷，詩人美之。及此，若曰：「君之使臣也，有勸功之典；臣之愛君也，有報德之誠。召虎於王何如哉？彼王念江漢之功也，蕃錫寵臨，彰榮世美，其策命可謂隆矣。虎也蒙自天之恩澤而俯拜，
translation_en:
…in Jun Chen—why was this? Yao and Shun inherited an age of harmony, whereas King Wu and the Duke of Zhou faced a time of transformation: their circumstances differed, that is all. Thus, those who govern must above all set the foundations right; those who discuss government must above all understand the circumstances.

Book of Odes
