title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
糟粕故常之說雖正亦迂故孔子於史野
之際求彬彬焉而嘆夏商之道不勝其敝
言貴損益之也夫言六藝者皆文也則皆
務實也而獨於射乎執事獨舉射爲問母
曰射禮廢而天下無男子欲以男子之道
望愚生乎蓋自弧矢之作始於黃帝侯明
之典載乎虞書事之盡禮樂而立德行者
莫若射以故聖王務焉及周之興牧野一
戎散軍郊射凡所崇三射之制立五善之
===
目澤以擇士侯以封侯郁乎盛矣然秦滅
典墳天子之禮見於周官略不備所僅僅
者諸侯二篇而已姑舉六官所載則有射
人以射法治射儀而司常共旌司裘共侯
歌節以樂師治正以司馬掌次張其耦次
太僕賛其弓矢而太史飾中舎筭各職所
事而不相奪明有司也天子將祭與諸侯
羣臣射而擇其賢者與於祭曰大射諸侯
朝于天子而天子與之射曰賓射天子勞
punctuated: 糟粕故常之說，雖正亦迂。故孔子於史野之際求彬彬焉，而嘆夏商之道不勝其敝，言貴損益之也。夫言六藝者皆文也，則皆務實也，而獨於射乎？執事獨舉射爲問，母曰射禮廢而天下無男子，欲以男子之道望愚生乎？蓋自弧矢之作始於黃帝，侯明之典載乎虞書，事之盡禮樂而立德行者莫若射，以故聖王務焉。及周之興，牧野一戎，散軍郊射，凡所崇三射之制，立五善之目，澤以擇士，侯以封侯，郁乎盛矣！然秦滅典墳，天子之禮見於周官，略不備，所僅僅者諸侯二篇而已。姑舉六官所載，則有射人以射法治射儀，而司常共旌，司裘共侯，歌節以樂師，治正以司馬，掌次張其耦次，太僕賛其弓矢，而太史飾中舎筭，各職所事而不相奪，明有司也。天子將祭，與諸侯羣臣射，而擇其賢者與於祭，曰大射；諸侯朝于天子，而天子與之射，曰賓射；天子勞
translation_en:
…the dregs of received doctrines: even if correct, they are impractical. Thus Confucius sought a harmonious balance between excessive refinement and rustic simplicity, and lamented that the ways of Xia and Shang could not overcome their accumulated defects. His point was that judicious subtraction and addition were essential. All the Six Arts involve cultural forms, and therefore all require attention to substance. Why should archery alone be singled out? You, honored examiner, have chosen archery alone for your question. Might you be saying [?] that, with the abandonment of archery rites, there are no true men in the realm, and hoping that this ignorant student will live up to the way of a man?

The making of bows and arrows began with the Yellow Emperor, and the precedent for manifesting virtue through shooting at targets [?] is recorded in the Book of Yu. No activity more fully embodies ritual and music while establishing virtuous conduct than archery; hence the sage kings devoted themselves to it. When the Zhou arose, a single campaign at Muye secured victory; the army was disbanded, and archery was practiced in the suburbs. They honored the institutions of the three forms of archery and established the five virtues associated with it. At the marsh palace, they selected worthy men; through shooting at targets, they invested lords. How splendidly these institutions flourished!

But Qin destroyed the canonical writings. The Son of Heaven’s rites appear in the Offices of Zhou, though the account is sketchy and incomplete; only two chapters concerning the feudal lords remain. Taking for the moment what is recorded under the six ministries, the Director of Archery regulated archery ceremonies according to the rules of shooting. The Director of Standards supplied the banners, and the Director of Furs supplied the targets. The Music Master provided songs to mark the rhythm, and the Minister of War maintained order. The Director of Tentage erected shelters for the paired archers, the Grand Equerry assisted with their bows and arrows, and the Grand Scribe embellished the tally receptacle and deposited the counting rods. Each official performed his own duties without encroaching on another’s: thus the responsibilities of the officials were clearly defined.

When the Son of Heaven was about to offer sacrifice, he shot with the feudal lords and assembled ministers, selecting the worthy among them to participate in the sacrifice; this was called the Great Archery Ceremony. When the feudal lords attended court before the Son of Heaven and he shot with them, this was called Guest Archery. When the Son of Heaven rewarded…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其使臣及與羣臣飲酒而射曰燕射國之
大事在祀故曰大而賓客燕息明有義也
以言六弓王弓弧弓天子之弓也合九而
成規唐弓大弓諸侯之弓也合七而成規
夾弓庾弓大夫之弓也合五而成規尊卑
統馭明有廣狹也以言八矢枉矢絜矢利
火射殺矢鏃矢利近射矰矢茀矢用諸弋
恒矢庳矢用諸散前後重輕明有利鈍也
大射之侯則王熊虎豹諸侯熊豹大夫麋
===
賓射之侯則王三侯五正諸侯二侯三正
卿大夫一侯二正燕射之侯則天子熊侯
白質象尊嚴也諸侯麋侯赤質象賓服也
大夫布侯畫以虎豹象變化也士布侯畫
以鹿豕象賤微也天子六諸侯四孤卿大
夫三爲耦判矣大射於郊賓射於朝燕射
於寢爲地分矣天子騶虞爲節樂官備也
諸侯貍首爲節樂會時也卿大夫采蘋爲
節樂循法也士采蘩爲節樂不失職也抑
punctuated: 其使臣及與羣臣飲酒而射，曰燕射。國之大事在祀，故曰大；而賓客燕息，明有義也。以言六弓，王弓、弧弓，天子之弓也，合九而成規；唐弓、大弓，諸侯之弓也，合七而成規；夾弓、庾弓，大夫之弓也，合五而成規。尊卑統馭，明有廣狹也。以言八矢，枉矢、絜矢利火射；殺矢、鏃矢利近射；矰矢、茀矢用諸弋；恒矢、庳矢用諸散。前後重輕，明有利鈍也。大射之侯，則王熊虎豹，諸侯熊豹，大夫麋；賓射之侯，則王三侯五正，諸侯二侯三正，卿大夫一侯二正；燕射之侯，則天子熊侯白質，象尊嚴也；諸侯麋侯赤質，象賓服也；大夫布侯畫以虎豹，象變化也；士布侯畫以鹿豕，象賤微也。天子六，諸侯四，孤卿大夫三，爲耦判矣。大射於郊，賓射於朝，燕射於寢，爲地分矣。天子《騶虞》爲節，樂官備也；諸侯《貍首》爲節，樂會時也；卿大夫《采蘋》爲節，樂循法也；士《采蘩》爲節，樂不失職也。抑
translation_en:
…his envoys, and when he drinks wine and shoots with his assembled ministers, this is called “banquet archery.” Sacrifice is a great affair of the state; hence the designation “great archery.” Receiving guests and enjoying repose likewise clearly have their respective meanings.

As for the six bows: the wang bow and hu bow are the Son of Heaven’s bows; nine joined together form a circle. The tang bow and great bow are the feudal lords’ bows; seven joined together form a circle. The jia bow and yu bow are the grandees’ bows; five joined together form a circle. The distinctions of superior and inferior, and of command and control, are thus clearly expressed through differences in breadth.

As for the eight arrows: wang arrows and jie arrows are suited to shooting with fire; killing arrows and pointed arrows [?] are suited to close-range shooting; zeng arrows and fu arrows are used for shooting birds with corded arrows; heng arrows and bi arrows are used for scattered shooting. Differences in the weight of the front and rear clearly distinguish their effectiveness.

For great archery, the king’s targets bear representations of bears, tigers, and leopards; those of the feudal lords, bears and leopards; and those of the grandees, elk. For guest archery, the king has three targets with five-colored aiming marks; the feudal lords have two targets with three-colored marks; and ministers and grandees have one target with two-colored marks. For banquet archery, the Son of Heaven has a bear target on a white ground, symbolizing dignity and majesty. The feudal lords have elk targets on a red ground, symbolizing submission as guests. Grandees have cloth targets painted with tigers and leopards, symbolizing transformation. Gentlemen have cloth targets painted with deer and swine, symbolizing lowly status.

The Son of Heaven has six pairs of archers, the feudal lords four, and solitary ministers, ministers, and grandees three: the distinctions in pairing are thus established. Great archery takes place in the suburbs, guest archery at court, and banquet archery in the residential chambers: the locations are thus differentiated. The Son of Heaven shoots to the rhythm of “The Zouyu,” celebrating the full complement of officials. The feudal lords shoot to “The Fox’s Head,” celebrating attendance at assemblies at the proper times. Ministers and grandees shoot to “Gathering Duckweed,” celebrating adherence to the rules. Gentlemen shoot to “Gathering White Southernwood,” celebrating the faithful discharge of their duties. And furthermore…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其器度品節之中而名位等威之義不章
章較著歟至其敎人之射則曰鄉射州長
春秋以禮屬民而射于序鄉大夫以五物
詢衆庶而射于庠是已要皆以禮將之謂
之禮射故曰其容比禮其節比樂又曰內
正外直持弓矢審固而後可以言中是其
敎也以德也非以射也故爲士者藏脩游
息於禮樂之間而不覺其漸漬陶鎔以成
德行先王之所爲敎者有其實而已周衰
===
禮廢列國兵爭主皮貫革之風相沿浸失
古制斯禮餼羊兩漢之間惟明帝辟雍一
行耳唐開元中頗嘗論著一曰射於射宮
一曰觀射於射宮而給事中許景先疏奏
罷之其後復行之安福樓下噫微矣宋淳
化間有司具圖而曰俟弭兵之日行之乾
道間駸駸討論又以舊制煩苛不可此不
幾於文實並廢者哉恭惟我
太祖高皇帝統一車書脩明禮樂洪武三年
punctuated:
其器度品節之中，而名位等威之義不章章較著歟？至其敎人之射，則曰鄉射。州長春秋以禮屬民而射于序，鄉大夫以五物詢衆庶而射于庠，是已。要皆以禮將之，謂之禮射。故曰：「其容比禮，其節比樂。」又曰：「內正外直，持弓矢審固，而後可以言中。」是其敎也，以德也，非以射也。故爲士者藏脩游息於禮樂之間，而不覺其漸漬陶鎔，以成德行。先王之所爲敎者，有其實而已。
周衰禮廢，列國兵爭，主皮貫革之風相沿，浸失古制，斯禮餼羊。兩漢之間，惟明帝辟雍一行耳。唐開元中，頗嘗論著，一曰射於射宮，一曰觀射於射宮，而給事中許景先疏奏罷之。其後復行之安福樓下。噫，微矣！宋淳化間，有司具圖，而曰俟弭兵之日行之。乾道間，駸駸討論，又以舊制煩苛不可。此不幾於文實並廢者哉？
恭惟我太祖高皇帝統一車書，脩明禮樂。洪武三年，
translation_en:
…within the specifications of its equipment and its graded observances, are not the principles of rank, status, and graded authority plainly manifest? As for archery used to instruct people, this was called district archery. The subdistrict chief assembled the people through ritual in spring and autumn and conducted archery at the local school; the district grand master consulted the populace according to five criteria and conducted archery at the district school. These are the practices in question. In all cases, ritual guided the activity, and thus it was called ritual archery. Hence it is said: “Their bearing accords with ritual, and their rhythm accords with music.” It is also said: “Only after being upright within and straight without, and holding bow and arrows carefully and firmly, may one speak of hitting the mark.” This instruction worked through virtue, not through archery itself. Thus scholars pursued their studies and cultivation, their recreation and rest, amid rites and music, unaware of how these gradually steeped and molded them into virtuous conduct. The instruction provided by the former kings possessed genuine substance, and that was what mattered.
As the Zhou declined, rites fell into disuse, and the competing states fought one another. The practice of making penetration of the hide target the chief concern perpetuated itself, and the ancient institutions were gradually lost. This rite survived only as a sacrificial sheep—a vestige of former observance [?]. Throughout the Former and Later Han, it was performed only once, by Emperor Ming at the Biyong imperial academy. During the Tang Kaiyuan era, there was some discussion and codification: one observance was called “shooting at the archery hall,” and another “watching archery at the archery hall.” But the Supervising Secretary Xu Jingxian submitted a memorial requesting their abolition. Later, the rite was again performed below Anfu Tower. Alas, how diminished it had become! During the Song Chunhua era, the responsible officials prepared diagrams, but said that they would await the cessation of warfare before putting the rite into practice. During the Qiandao era, discussion steadily gathered pace, yet the old regulations were again deemed too cumbersome and exacting to implement. Was this not tantamount to abandoning both form and substance?
Reverently we reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao unified axle widths and writing throughout the realm and restored and clarified rites and music. In the third year of Hongwu…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詔天下學校剏射圃射儀圖式著爲令凡成均
博士弟子及郡邑有司學官罔不治射蔚
然文明之會莫可尚焉夫置圃於學猶鄉
之射也而責之提調有司博士學官猶在
州長云爾但百餘年來諸生涵濡被服日
用繇之而不知其所爲教者不曰桑弧蓬
矢有事四方也則曰文事武備不忘危亂
也夫使章縫而得爲干城之資顧不美乎
然竊非其本也孔子曰興於詩立於禮成
===
於樂無他養之也諸生歌於斯習於斯又
射且學於斯吾知天機與制器相觸情性
與肌膚並融不亦樂乎樂則生生則不知
足之蹈手之舞此聖學也豈易易言哉是
故好學不倦旄期不亂以繹志也子爲子
鵠臣爲臣鵠以射已也此實我
太祖養士置射之微亦成周教人禮射之意也
至中間斟酌損益之制又有可言者要之
儀禮詳而今射儀易簡戒射張侯陳器定
punctuated:
詔天下學校剏射圃，射儀圖式著爲令。凡成均博士弟子及郡邑有司學官，罔不治射，蔚然文明之會，莫可尚焉。夫置圃於學，猶鄉之射也；而責之提調有司、博士學官，猶在州長云爾。但百餘年來，諸生涵濡被服，日用繇之，而不知其所爲教者。不曰桑弧蓬矢，有事四方也，則曰文事武備，不忘危亂也。夫使章縫而得爲干城之資，顧不美乎？然竊非其本也。孔子曰：「興於詩，立於禮，成於樂。」無他，養之也。諸生歌於斯，習於斯，又射且學於斯，吾知天機與制器相觸，情性與肌膚並融，不亦樂乎？樂則生，生則不知足之蹈、手之舞。此聖學也，豈易易言哉？是故好學不倦，旄期不亂，以繹志也；子爲子鵠，臣爲臣鵠，以射已也。此實我太祖養士置射之微，亦成周教人禮射之意也。
至中間斟酌損益之制，又有可言者。要之，《儀禮》詳，而今射儀易簡。戒射、張侯、陳器、定
translation_en:
…he decreed that schools throughout the realm should establish archery grounds, and promulgated illustrated forms of the archery ritual as regulations. From the erudites and students of the Imperial University to the responsible officials and school instructors of prefectures and counties, all attended to archery. This flourishing confluence of civilized accomplishments could not be surpassed. Establishing archery grounds in schools resembled the archery ceremonies of the ancient districts; entrusting responsibility to proctors, the officials concerned, erudites, and school instructors likewise resembled placing it with the ancient subdistrict chiefs.
Yet for more than a hundred years, students have been steeped in this practice and have followed it in their daily lives without understanding its educational purpose. They say either that the mulberry bow and fleabane arrows signify undertaking service in the four quarters, or that military preparedness must accompany civil pursuits, lest danger and disorder be forgotten. Surely it is good that scholars wearing their ceremonial caps should become capable of defending the state. Yet I venture to think that this is not the fundamental purpose. Confucius said: “Be stirred by the Odes, take your stand through ritual, and attain completion through music.” This means nothing other than nurturing people. Students sing here, practice here, and also shoot and study here. I know that their spontaneous natural impulses will interact with the fashioned implements, and that their dispositions and feelings will be harmonized with their bodies. Is this not joyful? Joy gives rise to vitality, and vitality makes the feet dance and the hands move unawares. This is the learning of the sages: how could it be discussed lightly? Thus, loving learning without weariness and remaining unconfused even in advanced old age come from unfolding one’s purpose. A son takes being a son as his target, and a minister takes being a minister as his target, thereby directing the shot toward himself [?]. This is indeed the subtle purpose behind our Taizu’s establishment of archery to nurture scholars, and also the intention behind the perfected Zhou order’s use of ritual archery to educate people.
As for the provisions that have undergone considered modification, there is more to be said. In general, the Book of Etiquette and Ceremonial is detailed, while the present archery ritual is straightforward and simple. Giving notice of the archery ceremony, setting up the target, arranging the implements, determining …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
耦大較同而士民俊秀大夫子弟以及品
爵高卑之射各有其位則昔所未具也自
行省而下衛府州而縣而學之射各有其
圖則昔所未睹也誘射請射取矢視筭大
較同而執旗六人掌于容後似與舉旌偃
旌者稍別中的者飲三爵中采者飲二爵
似與不勝立飲者迥殊狐鵠穇鵠之異采
亦崇卑異侯之旨而儀不設樂以射敎子
弟無燕禮也鹿中兕中之異器亦庠序異
===
射之遺而文無迎賓以射主長官無賓禮
也其同者實也其不同者文也我
太祖之所爲禮者適於宜而已夫生今而不遵
聖王之制者謂之悖好古而不得先王之心者
謂之泥悖者吾知其不敢也大抵仍襲儀
禮舊篇曲儒所見往往然爾寧不動執事
會通之思耶且如古人席地而坐坐而取
矢禮也今之坐不然矣必如古之人則使
尊賓皆跪以取矢將爲敬乎古者堂必有
punctuated:
耦，大較同，而士民俊秀、大夫子弟，以及品爵高卑之射，各有其位，則昔所未具也。自行省而下，衛、府、州而縣而學之射，各有其圖，則昔所未睹也。誘射、請射、取矢、視筭，大較同，而執旗六人掌于容後，似與舉旌、偃旌者稍別；中的者飲三爵，中采者飲二爵，似與不勝立飲者迥殊。狐鵠、穇鵠之異采，亦崇卑異侯之旨，而儀不設樂，以射敎子弟，無燕禮也。鹿中、兕中之異器，亦庠序異射之遺，而文無迎賓，以射主長官，無賓禮也。其同者，實也；其不同者，文也。我太祖之所爲禮者，適於宜而已。
夫生今而不遵聖王之制者，謂之悖；好古而不得先王之心者，謂之泥。悖者，吾知其不敢也。大抵仍襲《儀禮》舊篇，曲儒所見往往然爾，寧不動執事會通之思耶？且如古人席地而坐，坐而取矢，禮也。今之坐不然矣，必如古之人，則使尊賓皆跪以取矢，將爲敬乎？古者堂必有
translation_en:
…pairing the archers: these arrangements are broadly the same. Yet the outstanding men among scholars and commoners, the sons and younger relatives of senior officials, and archers of higher and lower official rank each have their assigned places—something not fully provided for in antiquity. From the Branch Secretariat down through the guards, prefectures, subprefectures, counties, and schools, each has a diagram for its archery ceremony—something not seen in antiquity. Demonstrating the shooting, inviting participants to shoot, retrieving arrows, and inspecting the counting rods are broadly the same. Yet the six flag-bearers stationed behind the protective screen seem somewhat different from those who raised and lowered the pennants. Those who hit the bull’s-eye drink three cups, and those who hit the marked area drink two: this seems quite different from the defeated archers’ drinking while standing. The different markings of the fox-hide and shen [?] bull’s-eyes likewise express the principle of using different targets for higher and lower ranks. But the ceremony provides no music, because this archery instructs sons and younger relatives and does not include the ceremonial banquet. The different deer-shaped and rhinoceros-shaped tally holders likewise preserve a vestige of the different archery ceremonies of the xiang and xu schools. But the written procedure contains no reception of guests, because the chief official presides over the shooting and there is no guest ritual. What is shared is the substance; what differs is the form. In establishing these rites, our Taizu simply made them appropriate to the circumstances.
To live in the present yet fail to follow the institutions of the sage king is called defiance; to love antiquity yet fail to grasp the intentions of the former kings is called rigidity. Defiance, I know, is something they would not dare commit. For the most part, they merely follow the old chapters of the Ceremonies and Rites: narrow-minded scholars often see things this way. Surely this should prompt you, sir, to consider how to reconcile the precedents and adapt them? For example, the ancients sat on mats on the ground, and taking up arrows while seated was the prescribed rite. Today we sit differently. If we must do as the ancients did, making all the honored guests kneel to retrieve their arrows, would that constitute respect? In antiquity, the hall invariably had…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
阼階及階揖升堂揖禮也今之階或不然
矣必如古之人而至畫地爲階以成三揖
非爲戲乎孔子射於矍相而使公罔之裘
揚觶子路延射蓋在觀射堵牆之時耳今
行之學宮則環而視之皆孝弟詩書之倫
烏有賁軍之將之可去也而必於揚觶不
已虛乎傳曰政不偕時固之敝也禮不從
宜執之愆也是故神而明之存乎其人而
我
===
太祖之制則固會通百王全善大美誠百世以
俟聖人不惑者也有志者儻實舉而行之
則所謂化裁通變之宜神明鼓舞之用其
盡在於斯夫抑愚言文而必求實者蓋言
體也言禮而必協宜者蓋語用也明體以
適用此正心誠意之學不可不講也今之
庠序豈惟游藝有弗若于古人毋亦志道
據德之功所未究心乎嗚呼文者質之衰
古人以六藝爲文君子曰非至文也乃至
punctuated: 阼階，及階揖，升堂揖，禮也。今之階或不然矣，必如古之人，而至畫地爲階以成三揖，非爲戲乎？孔子射於矍相，而使公罔之裘揚觶，子路延射，蓋在觀射堵牆之時耳。今行之學宮，則環而視之皆孝弟詩書之倫，烏有賁軍之將之可去也？而必於揚觶，不已虛乎？傳曰：「政不偕時，固之敝也；禮不從宜，執之愆也。」是故神而明之，存乎其人。而我太祖之制，則固會通百王，全善大美，誠百世以俟聖人不惑者也。有志者儻實舉而行之，則所謂化裁通變之宜，神明鼓舞之用，其盡在於斯夫！抑愚言文而必求實者，蓋言體也；言禮而必協宜者，蓋語用也。明體以適用，此正心誠意之學不可不講也。今之庠序，豈惟游藝有弗若于古人，毋亦志道據德之功所未究心乎？嗚呼！文者，質之衰。古人以六藝爲文，君子曰非至文也。乃至
translation_en:
…an eastern stairway for the host; bowing upon reaching the stairs and bowing upon ascending the hall were prescribed ritual. Today, stairways may be arranged differently. If we insist on following the ancients, even drawing stairways on the ground to complete the three bows, is this not playacting? When Confucius conducted archery at Juexiang and had Gongwang Zhiqiu raise the wine cup and Zilu invite people to shoot, this was at a time when spectators stood packed like a wall. Today, when the ceremony is held in the school precincts, those gathered around to watch are all people devoted to filial and fraternal duty and versed in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents. Where among them would there be a general whose army had fled, who must be excluded? To insist on raising the wine cup nevertheless—is this not empty ceremony? A transmitted text says: “When government does not keep pace with the times, this is the failing of rigidity; when ritual does not accord with what is fitting, this is the fault of obstinacy.” Thus, rendering these practices spiritually effective and intelligible depends upon the person who carries them out. The institutions of our Taizu comprehensively reconcile those of the hundred kings, embodying complete goodness and consummate excellence. Truly, they can await a sage a hundred generations hence without giving rise to doubt. If those with the resolve would actually put them into practice, then what are called the fitting means of transformation and adaptation, and the spiritually illuminating power to inspire and animate, would surely all be found here!

Yet when I speak of outward forms and insist on seeking substance, I am speaking of their underlying foundation; when I speak of ritual and insist that it accord with what is fitting, I am speaking of its practical operation. To understand the foundation so as to apply it appropriately requires the learning of rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere; this must be studied. In today's schools, is it only in cultivating the arts that people fall short of the ancients? Might they also have failed to devote their minds fully to setting their aspirations upon the Way and grounding themselves in virtue? Alas! Outward refinement is the waning of substance. The ancients regarded the Six Arts as refinement, yet the gentleman said that this was not the highest refinement. It has even reached the point that…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
併其六藝而學官寘之弗講弟子懵焉不
知而人士相語則曰文盛文盛是何哉所
謂文者執事其敎之
第四問
金文業
同考試官敎諭林批宗法所以明氏族世系
不淺場中蓋鮮知之子能稽古援經條分縷析是
誠究意于惇本之學者錄玆匪徒取其文焉爾
考試官敎諭黃批博物洽聞子誠足以當
===
之可敬
考試官學正林批條答無遺博古之學也
秩天下之大倫者莫先于族類之辯正族
類之大本者莫重于宗法之立夫氏族統
同於天下所以明有系也宗法別屬於一
家所以明有本也使宗法不立則氏族不
明氏族不明則昭穆紊矣親疎淆矣尊卑
貴賤無自而序且別矣天常人紀舛鑿錯
謬其何以遡流窮源循末探本使人倫之
punctuated:
併其六藝而學官寘之弗講，弟子懵焉不知，而人士相語則曰：「文盛，文盛！」是何哉？所謂文者，執事其敎之。

第四問
金文業

同考試官敎諭林批：宗法所以明氏族世系，不淺。場中蓋鮮知之，子能稽古援經，條分縷析，是誠究意于惇本之學者。錄玆匪徒取其文焉爾。

考試官敎諭黃批：博物洽聞，子誠足以當之，可敬。

考試官學正林批：條答無遺，博古之學也。

秩天下之大倫者，莫先于族類之辯；正族類之大本者，莫重于宗法之立。夫氏族統同於天下，所以明有系也；宗法別屬於一家，所以明有本也。使宗法不立，則氏族不明；氏族不明，則昭穆紊矣，親疎淆矣，尊卑貴賤無自而序且別矣。天常人紀，舛鑿錯謬，其何以遡流窮源，循末探本，使人倫之
translation_en:
…even the six arts are set aside by the educational officials and left untaught, while students remain ignorant of them. Yet when scholars speak to one another, they say, “Learning flourishes! Learning flourishes!” Why is this? As to what is called learning, may you, honored officials, instruct us.

Fourth Question
Jin Wenye

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The lineage system serves to clarify clans and their lines of descent; this is no shallow subject [?]. Few in the examination hall understand it. You have investigated antiquity and drawn upon the Classics, distinguishing each point and analyzing every detail. You are truly someone who has devoted thought to the learning that strengthens the foundations. This answer is selected for more than its literary merits alone.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Broad knowledge of things and extensive learning”—you truly deserve this description. Admirable!

Comment by Examiner Lin, School Director: Your answers address every point without omission. This is learning grounded in extensive knowledge of antiquity.

In ordering the great human relationships throughout the realm, nothing takes precedence over distinguishing kinship groups. In rectifying the fundamental basis of those groups, nothing is more important than establishing the lineage system. Clans unite people throughout the realm, making clear that they share a line of descent; the lineage system distinguishes affiliations within a single family, making clear that they have a common root. If the lineage system is not established, clan relationships remain unclear. If clan relationships remain unclear, the alternating generational order of zhao and mu becomes confused, and close and distant kin become mingled. There is then no means of ordering and distinguishing the senior and junior, the honored and lowly. With Heaven’s enduring norms and the guiding principles of human relationships distorted and confused, how can one trace the stream back to its source, follow the branches to discover the root, and cause human relationships to …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也殊途而同歸也矣堯爲君盡君道耳而欲爲
君者則之舜爲臣盡臣道耳而欲爲臣者則之
大匠誨人以規矩學者亦以規矩盡人而不則
聖人猶方員而不法規矩是謂聖人人倫之規
矩可也盡人之性所以盡己之性人倫之規矩
立而益以見人倫之至矣然規矩取至於外者
也聖人之至則在乎心非有待於外也是心也
人皆有之亦非有待於人也嗚呼外者器也心
者神也聖人神以立極則無待於規矩學者神
===
以盡倫則亦無待於聖人噫斯其至矣
同前
岑用賓
同考試官敎諭江批論人倫者非塵腐可厭
則牽纏不了是作意見超卓格裁高古用五倫而
能擺脫不鑿其必學力之到者矣
考試官敎諭黃批論學有此思致最邃倫
之士也
考試官學正林批自得之文
punctuated:
也，殊途而同歸也矣。堯爲君，盡君道耳，而欲爲君者則之；舜爲臣，盡臣道耳，而欲爲臣者則之。大匠誨人以規矩，學者亦以規矩。盡人而不則聖人，猶方員而不法規矩，是謂聖人人倫之規矩，可也。盡人之性，所以盡己之性；人倫之規矩立，而益以見人倫之至矣。然規矩，取至於外者也；聖人之至，則在乎心，非有待於外也。是心也，人皆有之，亦非有待於人也。嗚呼！外者器也，心者神也。聖人神以立極，則無待於規矩；學者神以盡倫，則亦無待於聖人。噫！斯其至矣！

同前
岑用賓

同考試官敎諭江批：論人倫者，非塵腐可厭，則牽纏不了。是作意見超卓，格裁高古，用五倫而能擺脫不鑿，其必學力之到者矣。

考試官敎諭黃批：論學有此思致，最邃倫之士也。

考試官學正林批：自得之文。
translation_en:
…different paths lead to the same destination. When Yao served as ruler, he merely fulfilled the Way of the ruler, yet those wishing to be rulers take him as their model. When Shun served as minister, he merely fulfilled the Way of the minister, yet those wishing to be ministers take him as their model. A master craftsman teaches others with the compass and square, and learners likewise use the compass and square. To fulfill one's humanity without taking the sage as a model is like making squares and circles without following the square and compass. Thus it is fitting to call the sage the compass and square of human relationships. Fully realizing the nature of others is the means of fully realizing one's own nature. Once the compass and square of human relationships are established, the utmost perfection of those relationships becomes still more apparent. Yet the compass and square seek perfection in something external; the sage's perfection resides in the heart and does not depend on anything external. This heart is possessed by everyone, and so neither does it depend on another person. Ah! What is external is an implement; the heart is numinous spirit. When the sage employs this spirit to establish the ultimate standard, he has no need to depend on compass and square. When the learner employs this spirit to fulfill human relationships, he likewise has no need to depend on the sage. Ah! This is indeed the utmost perfection!

Same as the preceding [topic].
Cen Yongbin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Those who discuss human relationships are either tiresomely stale or endlessly entangled in their arguments. This composition is outstanding in its insights and lofty and antique in its form. It draws on the Five Relationships yet manages to break free of constraints without forced interpretation. Surely this is an achievement attained through diligent learning.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: To discuss learning with such depth of thought marks a scholar most profoundly versed in human relationships [?].

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: A composition born of the writer's own understanding.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
昭貴世道之煕隆於天下也哉噫此宗法
之關于氏族者信其重乎請因明問而陳
之禮曰繫之以姓而弗别雖百世而婚姻
不通是先王氏族之重所以達天親之本
始昭人道之懿彜也故裴駰曰天子賜姓
命諸侯命族族者氏之别名也所以統繫
百世使不别也氏者所以别子孫之所自
出也是故以國氏者堯之後繼封於唐而
爲唐氏舜之後始封於虞而爲虞氏以至
===
齊魯秦吳氏是也以地氏者傅說築于傅
巖而爲傅氏東蒙主於蒙山而爲蒙氏以
至東郭北門氏是也氏以字者子桑子言
而龍氏容氏則以名焉氏以次者孟孫季
孫而五王續祈左史右史倉人庫人則以
族以官焉其義不亦徵乎以凶德氏者所
以著其惡而蛸也莽也非以凶德乎以吉
德氏者所以彰其善而冬日也老成也非
以吉德乎曰巫氏曰卜氏以技氏者也曰
punctuated: 昭貴世道之煕隆於天下也哉！噫！此宗法之關于氏族者，信其重乎！請因明問而陳之。《禮》曰：「繫之以姓而弗别，雖百世而婚姻不通。」是先王氏族之重，所以達天親之本始，昭人道之懿彜也。故裴駰曰：「天子賜姓命諸侯命族。」族者，氏之别名也，所以統繫百世，使不别也。氏者，所以别子孫之所自出也。是故以國氏者，堯之後繼封於唐而爲唐氏，舜之後始封於虞而爲虞氏，以至齊、魯、秦、吳氏是也。以地氏者，傅說築于傅巖而爲傅氏，東蒙主於蒙山而爲蒙氏，以至東郭、北門氏是也。氏以字者，子桑、子言，而龍氏、容氏則以名焉。氏以次者，孟孫、季孫，而五王、續祈、左史、右史、倉人、庫人則以族、以官焉。其義不亦徵乎！以凶德氏者，所以著其惡，而蛸也、莽也，非以凶德乎？以吉德氏者，所以彰其善，而冬日也、老成也，非以吉德乎？曰巫氏，曰卜氏，以技氏者也；曰
translation_en:
…to make manifest the flourishing of the age throughout the realm [?]! Ah! How weighty indeed is the bearing of the lineage system upon surnames and clans! Allow me to set this forth in response to your discerning question. The Book of Rites says: “They are linked by their surname and are not treated as separate; even after a hundred generations, they do not intermarry.” The former kings’ emphasis upon surnames and clans thus served to convey the original basis of natural kinship and to illuminate the admirable constant norms of human relations. Thus Pei Yin said: “The Son of Heaven bestows surnames, and the feudal lords designate lineages [?].” “Lineage” is another name for a clan designation: it binds together a hundred generations so that they do not become separate. A clan designation distinguishes the origins from which descendants spring.

Thus, among those who took their clan designation from a state, Yao’s descendants were subsequently enfeoffed in Tang and became the Tang clan; Shun’s descendants were first enfeoffed in Yu and became the Yu clan. The Qi, Lu, Qin, and Wu clans are further examples. Among those who took their clan designation from a place, Fu Yue built walls at Fuyan and became the ancestor of the Fu clan; Dongmeng presided over Mount Meng and became the ancestor of the Meng clan [?]. The Dongguo and Beimen clans are further examples. Those whose clan designations came from courtesy names include Zisang and Ziyan, whereas the Long and Rong clans derived theirs from personal names. Those whose clan designations came from birth order include Mengsun and Jisun; Wuwang and Xuqi [?], together with Zuoshi, Youshi, Cangren, and Kuren, derived theirs from lineages or offices. Is the significance of these distinctions not evident?

Those who took clan designations from wicked conduct did so to display their evil: were Xiao and Mang not named for wicked conduct? Those who took clan designations from virtuous conduct did so to manifest their goodness: were Dongri and Laocheng not named for virtuous conduct? The Wu and Bu clans took their designations from specialized skills; those called…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
竇氏曰所氏曰巫乙匠陶氏以事氏者也
他如楊孫賈孫則又以族系氏者焉惠叔
顏文武成宣以謚氏者也以至成公氏成
王氏王孫公孫氏則又以爵氏者焉其指
不亦邃乎故自是而姓氏之傳燦然博矣
三烏五鹿氏以志也如陳伯袁之後爲袁
氏齊公子高之後爲高氏衞公子衞孫之
後爲孫氏魯閔子騫之後爲騫氏非以美
之字爲氏者乎如文王封聃叔於沈後爲
===
沈氏晉穆公封成師於韓後爲韓氏晉獻
公封畢萬於魏後爲魏氏非以封之邑爲
氏者乎黃帝之子爲弓之長因爲張氏周
史佚世守其官因爲史氏平王少子有文
在手曰武因爲武氏金日磾獲匈奴祭天
因爲金氏是又以一時之事爲氏者也要
皆表功德明倫理亦未爲失道也至如吳
是因孔融之嘲而改儀曰是嵇康因嵇山
之家而改奚曰嵇束皙之避難也則改疏
punctuated: 竇氏、曰所氏、曰巫乙匠陶氏，以事氏者也。他如楊孫、賈孫，則又以族系氏者焉。惠、叔、顏、文、武、成、宣，以謚氏者也。以至成公氏、成王氏、王孫、公孫氏，則又以爵氏者焉。其指不亦邃乎？故自是而姓氏之傳燦然博矣。三烏、五鹿氏，以志也。如陳伯袁之後爲袁氏，齊公子高之後爲高氏，衞公子衞孫之後爲孫氏，魯閔子騫之後爲騫氏，非以美之字爲氏者乎？如文王封聃叔於沈，後爲沈氏；晉穆公封成師於韓，後爲韓氏；晉獻公封畢萬於魏，後爲魏氏，非以封之邑爲氏者乎？黃帝之子爲弓之長，因爲張氏；周史佚世守其官，因爲史氏；平王少子有文在手曰武，因爲武氏；金日磾獲匈奴祭天，因爲金氏。是又以一時之事爲氏者也。要皆表功德、明倫理，亦未爲失道也。至如吳是因孔融之嘲而改儀曰是，嵇康因嵇山之家而改奚曰嵇，束皙之避難也，則改疏
translation_en:
…the Dou clan, the Suo clan, and the Wu, Yi, Jiang, and Tao clans [?] took their clan names from activities. Other names, such as Yangsun and Jiasun, were derived from lineage. Hui, Shu, Yan, Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Xuan were derived from posthumous titles. Chenggong, Chengwang, Wangsun, and Gongsun were derived from noble rank. Are the meanings behind these not profound? From this point onward, the transmission of surnames and clan names became splendidly diverse. The Sanwu and Wulu clans took their names from identifying signs.

For example, the descendants of Boyuan of Chen became the Yuan clan; those of Prince Gao of Qi became the Gao clan; those of Prince Weisun of Wei [?] became the Sun clan; and those of Min Ziqian of Lu became the Qian clan. Were these not cases of taking an ancestor’s fine courtesy name as a clan name? King Wen enfeoffed Dan Shu in Shen, and his descendants became the Shen clan; Duke Mu of Jin [?] enfeoffed Cheng Shi in Han, and his descendants became the Han clan; Duke Xian of Jin enfeoffed Bi Wan in Wei, and his descendants became the Wei clan. Were these not cases of taking the name of an enfeoffed settlement as a clan name?

A son of the Yellow Emperor became chief of bow-making and consequently took Zhang as his clan name. Shi Yi of Zhou and his descendants held their office hereditarily and consequently took Shi as their clan name. King Ping’s youngest son had markings on his hand forming the character wu, and consequently took Wu as his clan name. Jin Midi obtained the Xiongnu’s object for sacrificing to Heaven [?] and consequently took Jin as his clan name. These, in turn, were cases of deriving clan names from particular events. In essence, all served to commemorate merit and virtue and clarify human relationships; they did not depart from the Way.

As for Wu Shi, he changed his surname from Yi to Shi because of Kong Rong’s mockery. Ji Kang changed his surname from Xi to Ji because his family lived at Mount Ji. When Shu Xi fled danger, he changed the surname Shu…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣之氏而為東賀循之避諱也則改慶譜
之氏而為賀此其率意更改以致後世之
莫辯者自是基之矣夏啟封支子於莘莘
後為華氏武王封虢叔於西虢後為郭氏
氏以聲近而訛也如邾子之後去邑而為
朱氏邘氏之後去邑而為于氏非以字近
而訛其姓者也如祁氏一族也凡六别其
姓媯氏一族也凡四别其姓非以姓多而
訛其族者乎杜氏一姓而有五望張氏一
===
姓而有十望劉氏一姓而有六望是又望
多而訛其姓者也要皆世遠裔繁音轉字
訛理勢所必然也至如安東王氏出於阿
布恩營州王氏出於高麗果可以附周齊
之後柳城李氏出於契丹代北李氏出於
沙陀李正巳出於高麗李寶臣出於奚種
寧可以紹臯陶之系此則因姓附人以致
君之姻誚者厥有所由矣故嬴秦滅學公
侯子孫失其本末司馬遷乃約世本脩史
punctuated:
廣之氏而為東；賀循之避諱也，則改慶譜之氏而為賀。此其率意更改，以致後世之莫辯者，自是基之矣。夏啟封支子於莘，莘後為華氏；武王封虢叔於西虢，後為郭氏：氏以聲近而訛也。如邾子之後，去邑而為朱氏；邘氏之後，去邑而為于氏：非以字近而訛其姓者也。如祁氏一族也，凡六别其姓；媯氏一族也，凡四别其姓：非以姓多而訛其族者乎？杜氏一姓而有五望，張氏一姓而有十望，劉氏一姓而有六望，是又望多而訛其姓者也。要皆世遠裔繁，音轉字訛，理勢所必然也。至如安東王氏出於阿布恩，營州王氏出於高麗，果可以附周齊之後？柳城李氏出於契丹，代北李氏出於沙陀，李正巳出於高麗，李寶臣出於奚種，寧可以紹臯陶之系？此則因姓附人，以致君之姻誚者，厥有所由矣。
故嬴秦滅學，公侯子孫失其本末，司馬遷乃約世本，脩史
translation_en:
…Guang’s surname to Dong [?]; when He Xun avoided a tabooed name, he changed Qing Pu’s [?] surname to He. Such arbitrary changes laid the foundation for the inability of later generations to distinguish these lineages. Qi of the Xia enfeoffed a younger son at Shen, and Shen’s descendants became the Hua clan. King Wu enfeoffed Guo Shu at Western Guo, and his descendants became the Guo clan: here clan names were corrupted through similarity of sound. Likewise, the descendants of the ruler of Zhu (邾) removed the ‘settlement’ component from the character and became the Zhu (朱) clan; descendants of the Yu (邘) clan removed that component and became the Yu (于) clan. Were these not cases in which surnames were corrupted through similarity of written forms? The Qi clan was one lineage, yet its surname branched into six; the Gui clan was one lineage, yet its surname branched into four. Were these not cases in which a multiplicity of surnames obscured the lineage? The single surname Du had five eminent regional lineages; Zhang had ten, and Liu had six. Here, again, a multiplicity of eminent regional lineages confused surnames. In general, as generations grew distant and descendants multiplied, pronunciations shifted and written forms became corrupted: these were inevitable developments.
As for the Wang clan of Andong, which descended from Abu’en, and the Wang clan of Yingzhou, which originated in Goryeo, could they really be attached to the descendants of Zhou and Qi? The Li clan of Liucheng originated among the Khitan; the Li clan of Daibei among the Shatuo; Li Zhengsi came from Goryeo, and Li Baochen from the Xi people. Could they possibly continue the lineage of Gao Yao? These were cases of claiming affiliation with others on the basis of a surname, thereby inviting ridicule concerning ‘your marriage connections’ [?]; there were reasons for this.
Thus, when the Qin of the Ying house destroyed learning, the descendants of dukes and marquises lost knowledge of their origins and descent. Sima Qian then abridged the Book of Genealogies (Shiben) and compiled the Records of the Historian …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
記因周譜以明世家而天下始知姓氏所
自焉至魏立九品官人之法官有世胄譜
有世官由是有譜局令史而氏族始有所
掌焉他則山東士人崇尚閥閱而高士廉
譜牒所由攷也博稽記載紀氏族者不可
以序別之乎應劭之作風俗通訛陋無稽
以至唐宋諸儒乃因陋踵誣沿襲不改實
劭之誤起之也歐陽脩之作宰相表精詳
有據以至九十三族如鍾陳韓高舛訛亦
===
甚殆脩之詳致之也他則姓苑冗雜考正
是非而林寶元和姓纂之由作也彼善於
此論氏族者不可以釐正之乎嗚呼李義
府不得與於李德宗之譜乃傳致其訛杜
正倫不能齒於杜城南之牒乃鑿摘其失
背本斁彜是何心也不寧惟是於王氏不
知其元城宜春郇城也於劉氏不知其陶
唐奉春元海也於馬氏不知其馬服馬矢
石氏不知其周術後趙也甚哉氏族未易
punctuated: 記，因周譜以明世家，而天下始知姓氏所自焉。至魏立九品官人之法，官有世胄，譜有世官，由是有譜局令史，而氏族始有所掌焉。他則山東士人崇尚閥閱，而高士廉譜牒所由攷也。博稽記載，紀氏族者不可以序別之乎？應劭之作《風俗通》，訛陋無稽，以至唐宋諸儒乃因陋踵誣，沿襲不改，實劭之誤起之也。歐陽脩之作《宰相表》，精詳有據，以至九十三族，如鍾、陳、韓、高，舛訛亦甚，殆脩之詳致之也。他則《姓苑》冗雜，考正是非，而林寶《元和姓纂》之由作也。彼善於此，論氏族者不可以釐正之乎？嗚呼！李義府不得與於李德宗之譜，乃傳致其訛；杜正倫不能齒於杜城南之牒，乃鑿摘其失。背本斁彜，是何心也？不寧惟是，於王氏不知其元城、宜春、郇城也；於劉氏不知其陶唐、奉春、元海也；於馬氏不知其馬服、馬矢，石氏不知其周術、後趙也。甚哉，氏族未易
translation_en:
…Records of the Historian, using Zhou genealogies to elucidate the hereditary houses; only then did people throughout the realm begin to understand the origins of surnames. When Wei established the nine-rank system for appointing officials, officeholders included descendants of hereditary families, and genealogies recorded hereditary officeholding. Thereupon clerks were appointed to genealogical bureaus, and clan lineages first came under official supervision. Furthermore, scholars of Shandong prized distinguished ancestry, which prompted Gao Shilian’s examination of genealogies. By consulting records extensively, could those recording clans not arrange and distinguish them?

Ying Shao’s Comprehensive Account of Customs was erroneous, crude, and unsupported by evidence. Even the scholars of Tang and Song perpetuated its inadequacies and falsehoods, transmitting them without correction: it was indeed Shao’s errors that began this. Ouyang Xiu’s Table of Chief Councilors was meticulous, detailed, and grounded in evidence; yet among its ninety-three clans, such as Zhong, Chen, Han, and Gao, discrepancies and errors were also considerable. Perhaps Xiu’s very pursuit of detail caused them. Elsewhere, the Garden of Surnames was prolix and confused; the effort to examine and correct its claims prompted Lin Bao to compile the Yuanhe Compilation of Surnames. Since one account is better than another, could those discussing clans not rectify their errors?

Alas! Li Yifu could not gain inclusion in Li Dezong’s genealogy [?], and so propagated its errors; Du Zhenglun could not be ranked within the genealogy of the Du clan south of the city, and so strained to pick out its faults. What sort of intentions led them to turn their backs on their roots and corrupt enduring moral norms? Nor was this all. Regarding the Wang clan, people do not distinguish its Yuancheng, Yichun, and Xuncheng branches; regarding the Liu clan, they do not distinguish its Tao Tang, Fengchun, and Yuanhai lines; regarding the Ma clan, they do not distinguish Mafu from Mashi [?]; and regarding the Shi clan, they do not distinguish Zhou Shu [?] from Later Zhao. How grievous it is that clans are not easily…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
辨也蓋係于譜牒之明廢而已故曰古之
氏族繁而知之者多今之氏族簡而知之
者寡其斯之謂歟雖然三代以前姓氏之
權出于上而譜牒為易明三代以下姓氏
之權出于下而譜牒為難考故遥遥華胄
聞者非焉汾陽一拜識者恥之寧非譜牒
之不講耶茲欲定譜牒明世系使是非出
于一定而天下知所以尊祖敬宗報本反
始如執事所謂倣成周小史之所職者頒
===
行天下則極建於上俗美於下本源澄而
支裔自清統系正而昭穆斯明矣棠棣行
葦之美不其復見于今乎故以此治國則
國有倫以此繫民則民不散豈不為同人
之道哉要之在宗法之立耳故曰宗法立
則人知重本而朝廷之勢自尊誠講明氏
族者所當注措焉
第五問
陳試
punctuated:
辨也，蓋係于譜牒之明廢而已。故曰：「古之氏族繁，而知之者多；今之氏族簡，而知之者寡。」其斯之謂歟？雖然，三代以前，姓氏之權出于上，而譜牒為易明；三代以下，姓氏之權出于下，而譜牒為難考。故「遥遥華胄」，聞者非焉；汾陽一拜，識者恥之。寧非譜牒之不講耶？茲欲定譜牒，明世系，使是非出于一定，而天下知所以尊祖敬宗、報本反始，如執事所謂倣成周小史之所職者，頒行天下，則極建於上，俗美於下，本源澄而支裔自清，統系正而昭穆斯明矣。《棠棣》《行葦》之美，不其復見于今乎？故以此治國，則國有倫；以此繫民，則民不散。豈不為同人之道哉？要之，在宗法之立耳。故曰：「宗法立，則人知重本，而朝廷之勢自尊。」誠講明氏族者所當注措焉。
第五問
陳試
translation_en:
…to distinguish. It depends simply on whether genealogical records are kept clear or allowed to fall into disuse. Thus it is said: “In antiquity, lineages were numerous, yet many understood them; today, lineages are few, yet few understand them.” Is this not what those words mean? Nevertheless, before the end of the Three Dynasties, authority over surnames rested with those above, so genealogical records were readily clarified; after the Three Dynasties, that authority rested with those below, so genealogical records became difficult to verify. Thus those who heard the claim to “illustrious ancestry in the distant past” condemned it, and knowledgeable people felt shame at the bow paid to Fenyang. Was this not because genealogical records had gone unstudied?

If we now wish to establish authoritative genealogical records and clarify lines of descent, ensuring that judgments of truth and error rest on a settled standard, and enabling everyone under Heaven to understand how to honor ancestors, respect the lineage, repay their origins, and return to their beginnings, then we should follow your proposal: emulate the duties of the Minor Scribe of the Zhou and promulgate this system throughout the realm. The highest standard would then be established above, and customs would improve below. Once the source was clear, its branches would naturally become pure; once the lines of descent were corrected, the zhao and mu generational order would become clear. Would not the excellence celebrated in “The Cherry Tree” and “The Reeds” appear again today? Thus, by governing the state through this system, the state would possess proper relationships; by binding the people together through it, the people would not disperse. Would this not constitute the way of fellowship among people?

The essential point is simply to establish the lineage system. Thus it is said: “Once the lineage system is established, people will know to value their roots, and the authority of the imperial court will naturally command respect.” This is indeed where those who seek to investigate and clarify lineages should direct their efforts.

Fifth Policy Question
Chen Shi

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張批平黎一策諸士類能言
之究理亂之源達失得之故於戰勝之外編戶治
之以理化之則子根本之論也錄之表經世之學
考試官教諭黃批經畫詳明區處允當是
必留心於平黎者矣
考試官學正林批具見匡時之略
人曰王者之不治夷狄也愚則曰未甞不
欲其治也人曰夷狄之不可理化也愚則
曰未甞不同此理也夷狄辟之禽獸然彼
===
惡知所謂理者求其大治必至於大亂故
以不治爲治也於戲天地萬物本吾一體
卽禽獸而聖人未甞不愛也鳥儀獸舞之
化是果何理哉而夷亦人類也其耳目口
鼻與人同其飲食男女與人同則其樂生
惡死趨利遠害之情猶人耳安得而不以
人治之王者所不治乃車書文物之外非
中土也今之黎峒地屬瓊海固中國之要
郡且黎內而民外其斯民腹心之疾也將
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張批：平黎一策，諸士類能言之。究理亂之源，達失得之故，於戰勝之外，編戶治之，以理化之，則子根本之論也。錄之，表經世之學。
考試官教諭黃批：經畫詳明，區處允當，是必留心於平黎者矣。
考試官學正林批：具見匡時之略。
人曰：「王者之不治夷狄也。」愚則曰：「未甞不欲其治也。」人曰：「夷狄之不可理化也。」愚則曰：「未甞不同此理也。」夷狄辟之禽獸，然彼惡知所謂理者？求其大治，必至於大亂，故以不治爲治也。於戲！天地萬物，本吾一體。卽禽獸，而聖人未甞不愛也。鳥儀獸舞之化，是果何理哉？而夷亦人類也，其耳目口鼻與人同，其飲食男女與人同，則其樂生惡死、趨利遠害之情猶人耳，安得而不以人治之？王者所不治，乃車書文物之外，非中土也。今之黎峒，地屬瓊海，固中國之要郡，且黎內而民外，其斯民腹心之疾也，將
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: On the policy of pacifying the Li, most candidates can offer an account. This essay investigates the sources of order and disorder and comprehends the reasons for failure and success. Beyond military victory, it proposes registering their households and governing them, transforming them through moral principle: this is your argument concerning the fundamentals [?]. We record it to display learning directed toward governing the world.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The planning is detailed and clear, and the proposed arrangements entirely appropriate. This must be someone who has devoted thought to pacifying the Li.

Comment by Examiner Lin, School Instructor: This fully reveals a strategy for remedying the troubles of the age.

Others say, “The true king does not govern the Yi and Di.” I humbly reply, “He has never ceased to desire that they be well governed.” Others say, “The Yi and Di cannot be transformed through moral principle.” I humbly reply, “They have never failed to share this same principle.” The Yi and Di are likened to birds and beasts: how could they know what is called moral principle? Seeking perfect order among them would inevitably bring great disorder; hence leaving them ungoverned is taken as the way to govern them. Alas! Heaven, earth, and the myriad things are fundamentally one body with me. Even birds and beasts have never been excluded from the sage’s love. Through what principle, indeed, does his transforming influence bring birds to appear in stately array and beasts to dance? Moreover, the Yi too are human beings. Their ears, eyes, mouths, and noses are the same as other people’s; their eating, drinking, and relations between men and women are the same. Their feelings—loving life and hating death, seeking benefit and avoiding harm—are thus just like those of other people. How could one fail to govern them as human beings? Those whom the true king leaves ungoverned lie beyond the reach of standardized carriages and writing and of civilized institutions; they are not within the central lands. The lands of today’s Li settlements belong to Qionghai, certainly an important commandery of China. Furthermore, the Li occupy the interior while the common people live around the outside: they are an affliction in the very heart and vitals of these people. Are we then to …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
毋治乎自昔平黎者曰撫曰戰曰守三者
之外無長策也至其言兵不曰機則曰權
曰略而已三者不言而言理書生之迂談
也三策不用而以治為策達士之駭聽也
然愚也本書生也故以書生之說進執事
於三策之外必得夫久安長治故以治之
之策進耳夫瓊顓顓大海之中三代以前
猶南服荒徼至漢元封始置珠崖儋耳二
郡繇是歷代更置不常而黎則嶋上蠻也
===
故有二種曰生曰熟生黎居內熟黎居外
要其居皆盤紆蒙密非人迹所窮俗稱黎
母山其最高處也一名五指峭若人指屹
立時時霧靄中故生黎所據尤峻險不可
迹任其狉獷不受欺觸賦役不供然不甚
出為民患為民患者熟黎耳熟黎耕省地
輸公稅而分隸四郡者也其初閩楚姦氓
蕩貲亡命及南恩藤梧高化從征之兵占
食其地因自稱峒首頭目而貪狡習兇始
punctuated:
毋治乎？自昔平黎者，曰撫，曰戰，曰守，三者之外無長策也。至其言兵，不曰機，則曰權、曰略而已。三者不言而言理，書生之迂談也；三策不用而以治為策，達士之駭聽也。然愚也，本書生也，故以書生之說進執事。於三策之外，必得夫久安長治，故以治之之策進耳。
夫瓊顓顓大海之中，三代以前猶南服荒徼。至漢元封，始置珠崖、儋耳二郡。繇是歷代更置不常，而黎則嶋上蠻也。故有二種，曰生，曰熟。生黎居內，熟黎居外。要其居皆盤紆蒙密，非人迹所窮。俗稱黎母山，其最高處也，一名五指，峭若人指，屹立時時霧靄中。故生黎所據尤峻險，不可迹，任其狉獷，不受欺觸，賦役不供，然不甚出為民患。為民患者，熟黎耳。熟黎耕省地，輸公稅，而分隸四郡者也。其初，閩楚姦氓蕩貲亡命，及南恩、藤、梧、高、化從征之兵，占食其地，因自稱峒首、頭目，而貪狡習兇。始
translation_en:
…are they to be left ungoverned? Since ancient times, those seeking to pacify the Li have advocated conciliation, warfare, or defense. Beyond these three, they have offered no lasting strategy. When discussing military affairs, they speak only of opportunities, expedients, and stratagems. To discuss principle without speaking of these three is the impractical talk of a bookish scholar; to employ none of the three strategies and instead make governance one's strategy is shocking to worldly men. Yet I, in my ignorance, am indeed a bookish scholar, and therefore present a scholar's views to you. Beyond these three strategies, we must find a means of securing enduring peace and lasting order. It is for this reason alone that I offer a strategy for governing them.
Qiong stands isolated [?] amid the great ocean. Before the Three Dynasties, it was still a remote frontier of the southern domains. Only in the Yuanfeng era of the Han were the two commanderies of Zhuya and Dan'er established. Thereafter, successive dynasties repeatedly altered their administrative arrangements. The Li are the island's native peoples, described as barbarians. They fall into two categories, called sheng, ‘unassimilated,’ and shu, ‘assimilated.’ The unassimilated Li dwell in the interior, and the assimilated Li on the periphery. In general, their settlements lie amid winding terrain and dense vegetation, beyond the full reach of human footsteps. What is commonly called Limu Mountain is the highest point; it is also called Wuzhi, ‘Five Fingers,’ its steep peaks resembling human fingers and towering frequently amid mist and haze. The territory occupied by the unassimilated Li is thus particularly precipitous and inaccessible. They are left to their rough and untamed ways, suffer no deception or encroachment, and furnish neither taxes nor labor service. Yet they seldom emerge to trouble the common people. Those who trouble the common people are the assimilated Li. These cultivate land under provincial administration, pay public taxes, and are apportioned among the jurisdictions of four prefectures. At the outset, unscrupulous people from Min and Chu who had squandered their wealth and become fugitives, together with soldiers from Nan'en, Teng, Wu, Gao, and Hua who had accompanied military campaigns, occupied this land and lived off it. They thereupon styled themselves ‘heads of dong settlements’ and ‘chieftains,’ but were greedy and cunning, and practiced violence. At first …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也賦役並供後駸駸不服差矣噫繇來漸
也竊迹往事觀之廣幅之調不堪遂攻郡
而殺守一也初元苦於久叛卒從棄郡之
請二也自吳以絕險不取至宋之南通無
功三也乾封瓊州之陷百二十四年而後
復四也紹定十年之亂郡城數十里莽爲
盜區五也至順之三軍既陷復寇乾寧而
澄邁隨之以破六也蓋其居勢彼高而我
下若與我爲主賓主則制人賓則制於人
===
此勝負之機也迨我
國朝
神功
聖烈四夷咸賓諸峒悉心歸附而崖州羅活等
峒間爲瓊患噫狐鼠耳於是辛丑大征蕩
然剗滅矣乃未十年復有今日之舉論者
咎之有司綏字失宜是誠然也然所釀長
積大之者又豈一朝一夕哉其言撫者在
昔固行之宋慶禮親諭首領釋讎相親李
punctuated:
也，賦役並供，後駸駸不服差矣。噫！繇來漸也。竊迹往事觀之，廣幅之調不堪，遂攻郡而殺守，一也；初元苦於久叛，卒從棄郡之請，二也；自吳以絕險不取，至宋之南通無功，三也；乾封瓊州之陷，百二十四年而後復，四也；紹定十年之亂，郡城數十里莽爲盜區，五也；至順之三，軍既陷，復寇乾寧，而澄邁隨之以破，六也。蓋其居勢，彼高而我下，若與我爲主賓，主則制人，賓則制於人，此勝負之機也。
迨我國朝神功聖烈，四夷咸賓，諸峒悉心歸附，而崖州羅活等峒間爲瓊患。噫！狐鼠耳！於是辛丑大征，蕩然剗滅矣。乃未十年，復有今日之舉。論者咎之有司綏字失宜，是誠然也。然所釀長積大之者，又豈一朝一夕哉？其言撫者，在昔固行之。宋慶禮親諭首領，釋讎相親，李
translation_en:
…they supplied both taxes and labor services, but later gradually ceased to comply with service levies. Alas! This developed by degrees. Examining past events, I observe the following. Unable to endure the levy of broad-width cloth [?], they attacked the commandery and killed its governor: this is the first instance. During the Chuyuan era, prolonged rebellion caused such distress that the request to abandon the commandery was finally accepted: this is the second. From Wu, which declined to take the territory because of its extreme ruggedness, down to Song, whose efforts to open communication southward achieved nothing: this is the third. Qiongzhou fell during the Qianfeng era and was recovered only after 124 years: this is the fourth. In the disturbances of the tenth year of Shaoding [?], the area extending for several tens of li around the prefectural city became a wilderness occupied by bandits: this is the fifth. In the third year of Zhishun, after the army had been overwhelmed, they again raided Qianning, and Chengmai subsequently fell as well: this is the sixth. The terrain they occupy places them above and us below, making them the hosts and us the guests. Hosts control others; guests are controlled by others. Here lies the determining factor in victory and defeat.
With the advent of our dynasty, its divine achievements and sagely exploits brought the barbarians of all four quarters into submission, and all the dong settlements pledged wholehearted allegiance. Yet Luohuo and other dong settlements in Yazhou occasionally caused trouble for Qiongzhou. Alas! Mere foxes and rats! Thus, in the xinchou year, a great expedition swept them away and utterly destroyed them. Yet fewer than ten years later, the present expedition has again become necessary. Those discussing the matter blame the responsible officials for failing to pacify and nurture the people properly. This is indeed true. But could the conditions that fostered and magnified the trouble have accumulated in a single morning or evening? As for those who advocate pacification, this certainly was practiced in the past. Song Qingli personally admonished the chieftains, leading them to set aside their enmities and become friendly with one another; Li…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
崇矩抵峒慰遺衆皆懷附朱國寶爲宣撫
使而降者三千戸涂棐爲副使而千家村
向化此具有成績者然非定計也一時兵
力未充姑蓄力有待如此耳其言戰者在
昔亦行之而於失得之際可三致嘆焉以
完澤新銳之兵當旣疲之寇勢若破竹而
納間受降此可伐不伐者也咸通四將所
向亡敵羣黎喘息待命而僅置忠州以還
此伐之不盡者也平章至元之師刋石五
===
指功勛偉甚然任用土人誘亂終元之世
此能伐而不能處者也三者旣失欲毋今
日得乎至言守者不過以斬伐之威未伸
招輯之恩難致而暫疆勉支吾之也斯又
下矣夫誕脩文德非撫乎然用之未事之
先者也豫無保釐之方俟叛而撫之是釀
亂也細柳堅壁非守乎然施之有備之際
者也本無制勝之策不得已而守之是示
怯也三者之中所須於今日燃眉之急戰
punctuated: 崇矩抵峒慰遺，衆皆懷附；朱國寶爲宣撫使，而降者三千戸；涂棐爲副使，而千家村向化。此具有成績者，然非定計也。一時兵力未充，姑蓄力有待，如此耳。其言戰者，在昔亦行之，而於失得之際，可三致嘆焉。以完澤新銳之兵，當旣疲之寇，勢若破竹，而納間受降，此可伐不伐者也。咸通四將，所向亡敵，羣黎喘息待命，而僅置忠州以還，此伐之不盡者也。平章至元之師，刋石五指，功勛偉甚，然任用土人，誘亂終元之世，此能伐而不能處者也。三者旣失，欲毋今日，得乎？至言守者，不過以斬伐之威未伸，招輯之恩難致，而暫疆勉支吾之也，斯又下矣。夫誕脩文德，非撫乎？然用之未事之先者也。豫無保釐之方，俟叛而撫之，是釀亂也。細柳堅壁，非守乎？然施之有備之際者也。本無制勝之策，不得已而守之，是示怯也。三者之中，所須於今日燃眉之急，戰
translation_en:
…Chongju went to the mountain settlements to offer consolation and gifts [?], and their inhabitants all willingly submitted. When Zhu Guobao served as Pacification Commissioner, three thousand households surrendered; when Tu Fei served as Vice Commissioner, Qianjiacun accepted civilizing rule. These measures all produced results, yet they were no settled strategy. Military strength was insufficient at the time, so they merely conserved their forces and waited for an opportunity—that was all.

As for warfare, it too was employed in the past, and its successes and failures give us three occasions for lament. Wanze’s fresh, keen troops faced an already exhausted enemy, advancing as readily as splitting bamboo; yet he accepted divisive counsel [?] and received their surrender. Here was an opportunity to attack that was not taken. The four generals of the Xiantong reign met no enemy who could withstand them; the Li people, gasping for breath, awaited their commands. Yet the generals merely established Zhongzhou and returned. Here was an attack not carried through to completion. The Administrator’s army in the Zhiyuan reign [?] inscribed its achievements on stone at Wuzhi: its exploits were truly magnificent. Yet the appointment of local men to office fomented disorder that continued to the end of the Yuan dynasty. Here was the ability to conquer without the ability to settle matters afterward. With these three failures behind us, could we possibly have avoided today’s situation?

As for those who advocate holding defensive positions, they merely reason that the might of punitive warfare has not yet been brought to bear and that the benevolence needed to win people over is difficult to extend; thus they temporarily struggle to hold things together [?]. This is an even poorer course. Was not the great cultivation of civil virtue a form of pacification? But it was employed before trouble arose. To have no means of securing and governing the region beforehand, and to wait until people rebel before pacifying them, is to foment disorder. Were not the firm fortifications at Xiliu a form of defense? But they were employed when preparations had already been made. To lack any plan for securing victory and take to defense only because there is no alternative is to display timidity. Of these three courses, what today’s emergency—as urgent as fire singeing the eyebrows—requires is warfare…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天下之道本一也聖人立其道為天下極者非
有以異於天下也夫非有異於天下天下以為
不可及而卒異之者天下自異之也惟天下之
自異也而後聖人之道立以法天下以傳後世
聖人始擅其異于天下抑孰知倫一道也道一
性也性一天也天下無二性而謂有二道哉道
不容以有二而聖人人倫之至亦盡乎天之所
以與我而先得乎人心之同初非有二也聖人
一其道而天下二之聖人同乎人而天下異之
===
則聖人脩道立極以一天下之二以同天下之
異其責有不容已矣蓋無所二者聖人之道也
無所異者聖人之心也憫天下之異而歸天下
之一者聖人之分也噫此聖人所以為人倫之
至也書曰天敘有典敕我五典五惇哉又曰惟
皇上帝降衷下民若有恒性克綏厥猷惟后夫
典自天敘性自降衷一也而惇之自我綏之惟
后一天下之二也天一之天下二之聖人一之
全乎天盡乎人而非聖人之異也自今觀之仁
punctuated:
天下之道本一也。聖人立其道為天下極者，非有以異於天下也。夫非有異於天下，天下以為不可及而卒異之者，天下自異之也。惟天下之自異也，而後聖人之道立，以法天下，以傳後世，聖人始擅其異于天下。抑孰知倫一，道也；道一，性也；性一，天也。天下無二性，而謂有二道哉？道不容以有二，而聖人人倫之至，亦盡乎天之所以與我，而先得乎人心之同，初非有二也。聖人一其道而天下二之，聖人同乎人而天下異之，則聖人脩道立極，以一天下之二，以同天下之異，其責有不容已矣。
蓋無所二者，聖人之道也；無所異者，聖人之心也；憫天下之異而歸天下之一者，聖人之分也。噫！此聖人所以為人倫之至也。《書》曰：「天敘有典，敕我五典五惇哉！」又曰：「惟皇上帝，降衷下民，若有恒性，克綏厥猷惟后。」夫典自天敘，性自降衷，一也；而惇之自我，綏之惟后，一天下之二也。天一之，天下二之，聖人一之，全乎天，盡乎人，而非聖人之異也。自今觀之，仁
translation_en:
The Way of all under Heaven is fundamentally one. When the sage establishes his Way as the supreme standard for all under Heaven, it is not because he possesses anything that sets him apart from everyone else. Though he is no different from them, people regard him as beyond their reach and ultimately set him apart: it is they who set themselves apart from him. Only because people thus set themselves apart is the sage’s Way subsequently established as a model for all under Heaven and transmitted to later generations; only then does the sage come to stand uniquely apart from the world. Yet who recognizes that what unifies human relationships is the Way, what unifies the Way is human nature, and what unifies human nature is Heaven? Since there are not two human natures in the world, can one say that there are two Ways? The Way admits of no duality. The sage, the highest fulfillment of human relationships, likewise merely fulfills what Heaven has bestowed upon us and apprehends before others what human hearts share in common. There was never any duality. The sage makes his Way one, but the world divides it in two; the sage is at one with other people, but the world sets him apart. Thus the sage cultivates the Way and establishes the supreme standard, unifying what the world has divided and bringing into common accord what the world has made different. This is a responsibility he cannot relinquish.
For the sage’s Way admits of no division; the sage’s heart admits of no distinction. To pity the world’s estrangement and restore it to unity is the sage’s allotted duty. Ah! This is why the sage is the highest fulfillment of human relationships. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven has ordered the constant norms; let us duly regulate our five norms, so that all five may be earnestly observed!” It also says: “The august Sovereign on High bestows an inner moral principle upon the people below. In accordance with this, they possess a constant nature; it is the ruler who can set them securely upon their proper course.” The norms derive from Heaven’s ordering, and human nature derives from the bestowal of the inner moral principle: these are one. Yet making those norms earnestly observed rests with us, and setting the people securely upon their course rests with the ruler: this is to unify what the world has divided. Heaven makes it one, the world divides it, and the sage makes it one again. He preserves whole what comes from Heaven and fully realizes what belongs to humanity; it is not that the sage is different. Viewed from this standpoint, benevolence…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其不可已乎或曰黎故無兵也頃緣一二
射利之徒以魚鹽為媒而潛授戈甲以販
商為號而遞報實虛故漢技得以資頑而
狼心易於鼓釁然則通貿之禁宜嚴而於
把隘之司加之意可乎或曰黎故不叛也
始壞於撫黎土職而終壞之土舍居則剝
黎以肥身變則間黎以阻化聞撫則格號
令將亂玉石之心聞征則泄事機自固輔
車之勢然則亟謫之防根蔕之深姑令率
===
其酋長聽有司之命可乎或曰莫先於開
道誠使於五指諸山東若牛嶺西若回風
乘此大眾之力而斬鉏草木燒赭藤蘿鑿
山通徑黎不得有其險矣是則然也然孰
與守之或曰莫要於屯田誠使於岐黎諸
峒申畫封疆設營置堡一倣屯兵之制而
多方招募願耕者聽民黎雜居黎不得專
其田矣是則然也然孰與制之眾建州邑
其開道屯田之完功乎蓋畫羣黎而版籍
punctuated:
其不可已乎？或曰：「黎故無兵也，頃緣一二射利之徒，以魚鹽為媒而潛授戈甲，以販商為號而遞報實虛，故漢技得以資頑，而狼心易於鼓釁。然則通貿之禁宜嚴，而於把隘之司加之意，可乎？」或曰：「黎故不叛也，始壞於撫黎土職，而終壞之土舍。居則剝黎以肥身，變則間黎以阻化；聞撫則格號令，將亂玉石之心；聞征則泄事機，自固輔車之勢。然則亟謫之，防根蔕之深，姑令率其酋長聽有司之命，可乎？」

或曰：「莫先於開道。誠使於五指諸山，東若牛嶺，西若回風，乘此大眾之力而斬鉏草木，燒赭藤蘿，鑿山通徑，黎不得有其險矣。」是則然也，然孰與守之？或曰：「莫要於屯田。誠使於岐黎諸峒，申畫封疆，設營置堡，一倣屯兵之制，而多方招募，願耕者聽，民黎雜居，黎不得專其田矣。」是則然也，然孰與制之？眾建州邑，其開道屯田之完功乎？蓋畫羣黎而版籍
translation_en:
…can it be dispensed with? Some say: “The Li originally had no weapons. Recently, however, one or two profit-seekers have used fish and salt as a means of access, secretly supplying weapons and armor, and have passed along intelligence about our strengths and weaknesses under the guise of trading. Thus Han skills have come to aid the recalcitrant, and wolfish hearts are readily stirred to provoke trouble. Should we therefore strictly enforce the prohibition on trade and give greater attention to the officials guarding the passes?” Others say: “The Li originally were not rebellious. The trouble began with the native officials charged with pacifying the Li and was brought to its culmination by the heirs of the native chieftains. In ordinary times they exploit the Li to enrich themselves; in times of disturbance they sow dissension among the Li to obstruct their transformation. When they hear of pacification, they obstruct orders, seeking to unsettle people with fears that jade and stone will perish alike [?]. When they hear of a punitive expedition, they divulge its plans, securing their own position through mutual dependence, like cheekbone and jaw. Should we therefore promptly banish them to prevent their roots from growing deeper, and provisionally have the Li follow their own chiefs in obeying the responsible officials?”

Some say: “Nothing takes precedence over opening roads. If, throughout the Wuzhi mountains—at places such as Niuling in the east and Huifeng in the west—we truly used the strength of this great host to cut down vegetation, burn away vines and creepers, and hew paths through the mountains, the Li could no longer command these natural defenses.” That is indeed so; but who would help guard them? Others say: “Nothing is more essential than agricultural colonies. If, throughout the valley settlements of the Qili, we truly redrew boundaries, established camps and forts, followed the military agricultural system in every respect, and recruited settlers by various means, permitting those willing to cultivate to do so, then commoners and Li would live intermingled, and the Li could no longer possess their fields exclusively.” That is indeed so; but who would help keep them under control? Would establishing numerous subprefectures and counties bring the opening of roads and the establishment of agricultural colonies to completion? For, by demarcating the various Li communities and entering them in the registers…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之治之功孰大於此然不易言也又聞
黎椎髻跣足寢食不釋弓絶無人禮至其
重契箭謹然諾錙銖不爽呿呿吁吁棧居
而蓬處其庶乎敦樸渾龐之風歟昔人有
言太古不可見蓋於黎獠彷佛焉噫傷之
者至矣誠使建州編户之後徧置塾學日
夕誨諭子弟而擇其耳目聰明納之黌宮
紓徐於衣冠之列吾知真性呈而天機悟
也若有奪夫弓矢之好攜而翼之漸而灌
===
之不利於速成不貪於近名不安於小康
於斯時也誰復與黎哉此謂以理化之者
也尤不易言也於戲戰勝之策效在目前
治之者非假之歲年不可高宗伐鬼方三
年克之其百世之功乎百世之功未足言
也王者必世而后仁使黎而歸仁焉其萬
世之功乎噫要皆書生之說也執事儻不
以其說爲迂則豈惟治黎哉則豈惟治黎
哉
punctuated: 之。治之功，孰大於此？然不易言也。又聞黎椎髻跣足，寢食不釋弓，絶無人禮。至其重契箭，謹然諾，錙銖不爽，呿呿吁吁，棧居而蓬處，其庶乎敦樸渾龐之風歟？昔人有言：「太古不可見，蓋於黎獠彷佛焉。」噫！傷之者至矣！誠使建州編户之後，徧置塾學，日夕誨諭子弟，而擇其耳目聰明，納之黌宮，紓徐於衣冠之列，吾知真性呈而天機悟也。若有奪夫弓矢之好，攜而翼之，漸而灌之，不利於速成，不貪於近名，不安於小康，於斯時也，誰復與黎哉？此謂以理化之者也，尤不易言也。於戲！戰勝之策，效在目前；治之者，非假之歲年不可。高宗伐鬼方，三年克之，其百世之功乎？百世之功未足言也。王者必世而后仁，使黎而歸仁焉，其萬世之功乎？噫！要皆書生之說也。執事儻不以其說爲迂，則豈惟治黎哉！則豈惟治黎哉！
translation_en:
…them. What achievement in governing them could be greater than this? Yet this is not lightly spoken of. I have also heard that the Li wear their hair in mallet-shaped knots and go barefoot, never putting aside their bows even when sleeping or eating, and entirely lack civilized propriety. Yet they honor pledges made with arrows, scrupulously keep their promises, and deviate from them not the slightest bit. With mouths agape and sighing [?], dwelling on raised platforms and sheltering beneath thatch, do they not approach the simple, honest, and unspoiled ways of antiquity? Someone of old said: “We cannot see remote antiquity, but among the Li and Liao we may glimpse its likeness.” Alas! How profound his sorrow for them!

If, after establishing subprefectures and registering households, village schools were set up everywhere, and their children instructed morning and evening; if those with keen faculties were selected and admitted to the schools, to mingle at ease among the capped and robed, I know that their true nature would emerge and their innate understanding awaken. If their fondness for bows and arrows could thus be displaced, one should lead and support them, gradually steeping and nourishing them in instruction, seeking no advantage in rapid accomplishment, coveting no immediate reputation, and resting content with no modest measure of peace. At such a time, who would still count them as Li [?]? This is what is meant by transforming them through moral principle. It is even less lightly spoken of.

Alas! A strategy for victory in battle produces results before our eyes; governing them requires years. Gaozong attacked Guifang and conquered it in three years: was this an achievement for a hundred generations? Even an achievement for a hundred generations is insufficient to speak of here. “Even with a true king, a generation must pass before benevolent rule prevails.” If the Li could be brought to embrace benevolence, would this not be an achievement for ten thousand generations? Alas! These are, after all, merely a scholar’s words. If you, sir, do not consider these words impractical, then surely they apply to more than governing the Li! Surely they apply to more than governing the Li!

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
惟茲鄉試御史以代至孔邇
庶工朋作茲乃先事考慎勞
於夙夜既戒既敘將卽事會
督府司馬偕總兵平江伯奉
命討亂於黎戈船十萬席捲南行
洗兵廣海之間刷馬越臺之
===
上御史介兩府賓館贊揚
威命商校武事敘戎憬夷本末具
舉既而曰有嚴有翼共武之
服共武之服以定王國督府
亦申意文塲討論厥事綢繆
於詩書之敦究極乎賓興之
典既而曰我覯之子維其有
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

惟茲鄉試，御史以代至孔邇，庶工朋作，茲乃先事考慎，勞於夙夜。既戒既敘，將卽事，會督府司馬偕總兵平江伯奉命討亂於黎，戈船十萬，席捲南行，洗兵廣海之間，刷馬越臺之上。御史介兩府賓館，贊揚威命，商校武事，敘戎憬夷，本末具舉。既而曰：「有嚴有翼，共武之服。共武之服，以定王國。」督府亦申意文塲，討論厥事，綢繆於詩書之敦，究極乎賓興之典。既而曰：「我覯之子，維其有
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

For this Provincial Examination, the censor had very recently arrived to take over his post [?]. The various officers worked together, carefully examining the arrangements beforehand and laboring morning and night. Instructions had been issued and duties assigned, and proceedings were about to begin when the governor-general, bearing a military ministerial title (dufu sima), together with the Regional Commander, the Earl of Pingjiang, received orders to suppress unrest among the Li. A hundred thousand warships swept southward; they washed their weapons in the waters of Guanghai and groomed their horses upon the terrace of Yue. The censor attended the two commanders at the guest lodge [?], extolling the august imperial command and discussing military affairs. In recounting the campaign and the distant Yi peoples [?], they addressed its origins and consequences in full. Then he said: “With solemnity and reverence, fulfill your military service. Fulfill your military service, thereby bringing stability to the royal realm.”

The governor-general likewise expressed his concern for the examination grounds and discussed their affairs, making careful preparations to foster devotion to the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, and thoroughly investigating the rites for honoring and recommending worthy men. Then he said: “I behold this man; indeed, he possesses …”

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
章維其有章是以有慶於時
文武將吏咸在登降燕勞詞
訓兼備威儀孔多士獲覩玆
盛際咸願奮揚惟曰
國家所以甄材命官文武兼資
久而益隆之道庶其在此惟
士所以恒旣厥心思以一日
===
自見以無負於
國家緩急有賴庶其在此乃咸
啓發憤悱大放厥詞至於其
日殆若觀兵涿鹿校戰昆陽
一怒未湼屢鼓不衰至皆引
筆盡紙繩而不輟探亹亹之
思順疊疊之意其精神所搆
punctuated: 章，維其有章，是以有慶。」於時，文武將吏咸在，登降燕勞，詞訓兼備，威儀孔多。士獲覩玆盛際，咸願奮揚，惟曰：「國家所以甄材命官，文武兼資，久而益隆之道，庶其在此。惟士所以恒旣厥心思，以一日自見，以無負於國家緩急有賴，庶其在此。」乃咸啓發憤悱，大放厥詞。至於其日，殆若觀兵涿鹿，校戰昆陽，一怒未湼，屢鼓不衰。至皆引筆盡紙，繩而不輟，探亹亹之思，順疊疊之意，其精神所搆
translation_en:
…distinction; because he has distinction, there is thus cause for rejoicing.” At that time, civil and military officers and their subordinates were all present. As they ascended and descended in ceremony and were entertained and rewarded, formal addresses and admonitions were both fully provided, and ceremonial dignity was abundantly displayed. The scholars, privileged to witness this splendid occasion, all wished to rouse themselves to greater effort. They declared: “Here, perhaps, lies the means by which the state selects talent and appoints officials, draws upon both civil and military abilities, and grows ever more flourishing with time. Here, perhaps, also lies the means by which scholars may continually devote their minds to the utmost, so that one day they may demonstrate their abilities and not disappoint the state's reliance upon them in ordinary times and emergencies.”
They therefore all gave expression to thoughts they had struggled to comprehend and articulate, freely pouring forth their words. When the day arrived, it was almost like reviewing troops at Zhuolu or engaging in battle at Kunyang: their first surge of ardor remained undiminished [?], and repeated drumbeats brought no slackening. All took up their brushes and covered their paper, continuing without pause [?], probing their unflagging thoughts and following their successive ideas—what their minds and spirits fashioned…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也蓋有聞聲響赴跡涉之而
影從者卽是殆無弗能於言
者矣而其雄偉非常信如所
云有摧陷廓清之象斯殆有
所感會矣文與武交賛而成
功者也兆是役矣詩云濟濟
多士克廣德心桓桓于征狄
===
彼東南其斯之謂歟旣事官
師交賀人懷好音雖諸士之
心其獲與是選亦誰不樂此
者而玉藻猥以無能獲承是
役惟一日之覯不可易是以
有愛願無已之心謂諸士時
則旣嘉矣言則旣從矣事則
punctuated:
也。蓋有聞聲響赴、跡涉之而影從者，卽是殆無弗能於言者矣。而其雄偉非常，信如所云有摧陷廓清之象，斯殆有所感會矣。文與武交賛而成功者也，兆是役矣。詩云：「濟濟多士，克廣德心。桓桓于征，狄彼東南。」其斯之謂歟？
旣事，官師交賀，人懷好音。雖諸士之心，其獲與是選，亦誰不樂此者？而玉藻猥以無能，獲承是役，惟一日之覯不可易，是以有愛願無已之心。謂諸士：時則旣嘉矣，言則旣從矣，事則
translation_en:
…indeed. There were, it seems, those who heard the sound and answered like an echo, who followed the tracks like a shadow [?]; thus there was scarcely anything they could not express in words. Their extraordinary grandeur truly displayed what has been called the power to break through defenses and sweep all clear. Surely this arose from something that stirred them and met with a response within. Civil and martial accomplishments support one another in achieving success: this examination has revealed the first signs of that. The Book of Odes says: “The many worthy men can broaden their virtuous hearts. Valiant on campaign, they bring order to the southeast.” Does this not describe the present occasion?
When the proceedings were over, the officials congratulated one another, and everyone cherished the good news. Among the candidates themselves, who, having gained a place in this selection, would not rejoice? And I, Yuzao, despite my lack of ability, had the undeserved privilege of undertaking this duty. Reflecting that this single day's encounter cannot be replaced, I feel unending affection and hope for them. I say to the candidates: the time has indeed been auspicious; your words have indeed found acceptance; as for your undertakings, …

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
旣合矣亦姑務大其所存而
已循緝於感會之餘發皇於
耳目之表究文武之所用效
將相於他日俾後之人考其
由來徵是舉焉不益美歟詩
曰文武吉甫萬邦爲憲
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教
===
諭黃玉藻謹序
punctuated:
旣合矣，亦姑務大其所存而已。循緝於感會之餘，發皇於耳目之表，究文武之所用，效將相於他日，俾後之人考其由來，徵是舉焉，不益美歟？《詩》曰：「文武吉甫，萬邦爲憲。」
江西吉安府萬安縣儒學教諭黃玉藻謹序。
translation_en:
…have already accorded. For now, simply strive to enlarge what you hold within. Continue cultivating it in the wake of this auspicious encounter, and bring it to full expression beyond what the ears and eyes can apprehend. Explore to the utmost the applications of civil and military learning, and in days to come render service as generals and chief ministers. Let later generations, investigating the origins of your achievements, find their evidence in this examination. Would this not be finer still? The Book of Odes says: “Civil and martial is Jifu; he is a model for the myriad states.”
Preface respectfully composed by Huang Yuzao, Instructor in the Confucian School of Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
得之元義得之利序別信得之亨貞聖人之於
人一也相臨也而君而臣相親也而父而子相
聯相儷相際也而兄弟而夫婦而朋友聖人之
於人一也仁行之於父子義行之於君臣序別
信行之於兄弟夫婦朋友聖人之於人一也但
物之感人無窮人之應物無節以無節之應而
遂無窮之感則心以氣昏性以情鑿道以欲蔽
而一者二矣是故賢智者過乎一者也愚不肖
者不及乎一者也仁者見之謂仁智者見之謂
===
智偏乎一者也夫道本一也而偏焉而過不及
焉二也道之不明不行也我知之矣而得謂之
至哉惟聖人者清明在躬志氣如神氣通極於
性性通極於命命通極于天是故其未發也涵
之於五性也天神天明天精天粹倫之體所以
立也雖鬼神莫窺其際矣而何其至乎猶未也
發之於五品也以篤父子以正君臣以睦兄弟
以和夫婦以孚朋友不思不勉無過無不及倫
之用所以行也雖天地莫與其能矣而何其至
punctuated:
得之元，義得之利，序別信得之亨貞。聖人之於人，一也。相臨也而君而臣，相親也而父而子，相聯相儷相際也而兄弟而夫婦而朋友，聖人之於人，一也。仁行之於父子，義行之於君臣，序別信行之於兄弟夫婦朋友，聖人之於人，一也。但物之感人無窮，人之應物無節，以無節之應而遂無窮之感，則心以氣昏，性以情鑿，道以欲蔽，而一者二矣。是故賢智者過乎一者也，愚不肖者不及乎一者也。仁者見之謂仁，智者見之謂智，偏乎一者也。夫道本一也，而偏焉，而過不及焉，二也。道之不明不行也，我知之矣，而得謂之至哉？

惟聖人者，清明在躬，志氣如神，氣通極於性，性通極於命，命通極于天。是故其未發也，涵之於五性也，天神天明，天精天粹，倫之體所以立也。雖鬼神莫窺其際矣，而何其至乎！猶未也。發之於五品也，以篤父子，以正君臣，以睦兄弟，以和夫婦，以孚朋友，不思不勉，無過無不及，倫之用所以行也。雖天地莫與其能矣，而何其至
translation_en:
…derives it from origination; righteousness derives it from benefit; proper order, distinction, and trustworthiness derive it from flourishing and constancy. The sage, in relation to other people, is one and undivided. In their relations of authority, people are ruler and minister; in their relations of affection, father and son; in their bonds, pairings, and dealings with one another, elder and younger brothers, husband and wife, and friends. The sage, in relation to other people, is one and undivided. Benevolence is practiced between father and son, righteousness between ruler and minister, and proper order, distinction, and trustworthiness between brothers, spouses, and friends. The sage, in relation to other people, is one and undivided. Yet things affect people without end, and people respond to things without restraint. When unrestrained responses pursue endless stimuli, the mind is clouded by vital energy, human nature is eroded by emotions, and the Way is obscured by desires: what was one becomes divided. Thus the worthy and intelligent go beyond this unity, while the foolish and unworthy fall short of it. The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. These are partial views of that unity. The Way is fundamentally one; taking a partial view of it, exceeding it, or falling short of it creates division. I know now why the Way is neither understood nor practiced. Can this be called the utmost attainment?

Only the sage embodies purity and clarity, with purpose and vital energy that are spiritlike. His vital energy communicates fully with his nature, his nature with his heavenly mandate, and his heavenly mandate with Heaven. Thus, before his feelings are aroused, he holds this within the five moral qualities of his nature: Heaven’s numinous power, Heaven’s illumination, Heaven’s refinement, and Heaven’s purity. This is how the underlying substance of human relationships is established. Even ghosts and spirits cannot discern its bounds. How consummate it is! Yet this is still not all. When expressed in the five human relationships, it deepens affection between father and son, rectifies relations between ruler and minister, fosters concord between brothers, brings harmony between husband and wife, and establishes trust between friends. Without deliberation or effort, with neither excess nor deficiency, the functioning of human relationships is thereby carried out. Even Heaven and Earth cannot match this capacity. And how consummate…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎猶未也達之於五教也表儀以樹藝極以陳
聲名以發文物以紀刑政以一官師以徇盡己
盡人存神過化倫之功所以極也而天下後世
莫能加毫末於此矣而何其至乎是故父子正
仁而天下父父子子者取衷焉君臣止義而天
下君君臣臣者取衷焉兄弟夫婦朋友止於序
別信而天下夫夫婦婦兄兄弟弟友友者取衷
焉激之不能使之高抑之不能使之卑小者而
不能加益大者而不能加損天下見聖人如是
===
而不可加也則曰聖人天之所厚而非人之所
同而其人倫之至真若天墜地出而震其異於
天下孰知聖人非求異天下也自其人之同者
充之亦非得厚于天也自其天之與者盡之故
曰性一天也道一性也倫一道也道一而天下
二之始見聖人爲不可及而以人倫之至異聖
人聖人豈有心以人倫獨異于天下哉天下之
道本一也聖人一其所一一天下之不一而已
一其所一者聖人無異天下之心也無一而無
punctuated: 乎？猶未也。達之於五教也，表儀以樹，藝極以陳，聲名以發，文物以紀，刑政以一，官師以徇，盡己盡人，存神過化，倫之功所以極也。而天下後世莫能加毫末於此矣，而何其至乎！是故父子正仁，而天下父父子子者取衷焉；君臣止義，而天下君君臣臣者取衷焉；兄弟夫婦朋友止於序別信，而天下夫夫婦婦兄兄弟弟友友者取衷焉。激之不能使之高，抑之不能使之卑，小者而不能加益，大者而不能加損。天下見聖人如是而不可加也，則曰聖人天之所厚，而非人之所同，而其人倫之至，真若天墜地出，而震其異於天下。孰知聖人非求異天下也，自其人之同者充之；亦非得厚于天也，自其天之與者盡之。故曰：性一天也，道一性也，倫一道也。道一而天下二之，始見聖人爲不可及，而以人倫之至異聖人。聖人豈有心以人倫獨異于天下哉？天下之道本一也，聖人一其所一，一天下之不一而已。一其所一者，聖人無異天下之心也。無一而無
translation_en: …how consummate it is! Yet this is still not all. When extended to the five teachings, exemplary standards are established, the standards of accomplishment are set forth [?], musical sounds and designations give them expression, cultural forms and objects give them ordered embodiment, punishments and government unify them, and officials and teachers carry them forth. Fulfilling both oneself and others, preserving the spiritual potency within and transforming wherever one passes: thus the achievement of human relationships reaches its utmost. Neither the world nor later generations can add the slightest thing to this. How consummate it is! Thus fathers and sons are set right in benevolence, and all under Heaven who act as fathers and sons take their proper measure from this. Rulers and ministers abide in righteousness, and all who act as rulers and ministers take their proper measure from this. Elder and younger brothers, husbands and wives, and friends abide respectively in due order, distinction, and trustworthiness; and all who act as husbands and wives, elder and younger brothers, and friends take their proper measure from this. Rousing it cannot make it higher; pressing it down cannot make it lower. In its smaller aspects nothing can be added, and in its greater aspects nothing can be subtracted [?]. Seeing that the sage is thus unsurpassable, people say that Heaven has especially favored him and that he does not share what is common to others. His consummate realization of human relationships truly seems to have fallen from Heaven or sprung from the earth, astounding the world with its strangeness. Who understands that the sage does not seek to differ from the world? He merely develops fully what he shares with other people. Nor has he received special favor from Heaven: he merely fulfills what Heaven has bestowed upon him. Hence it is said: human nature is one with Heaven; the Way is one with human nature; human relationships are one with the Way. The Way is one, but people divide it in two. Only then do they regard the sage as beyond reach and treat him as different because of his consummate realization of human relationships. Could the sage deliberately seek to stand apart from the world through human relationships? The Way of all under Heaven is fundamentally one. The sage unifies what is already one and brings unity to what is divided in the world—that is all. In unifying what is already one, the sage has no intention of differing from the world. There is no single unity, yet there is no…

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不一者聖人同天下之分也蓋至此則天下之
偏乎一過不及乎一者皆歸於聖人之一矣而
聖人盡倫立道之效至於天地訢合萬物昭蘇
橫四海塞天地施之後世而無不一矣易曰天
下之動貞夫一者也裁成天地之道輔相天地
之宜一之至也聖人與天地參矣又如之何其
可及也嘗聞之聖可學乎一爲要一者無欲無
欲則靜虛動直靜虛則明而人倫之理洞然於
吾心而無所蔽動直則公而人倫之理渾然於
===
吾身而無所虧勿助勿忘兩忘俱化是亦聖人
之一也孟子曰堯舜性之也人皆可以爲堯舜
噫知堯舜之可爲則知聖人之可學矣
表
擬宋司馬光進十科舉士法表〔元祐元年〕
陳試
同考試官教諭張批四六自歐陽諸公始一
變俳體典則雅正至以屬對律切敘事陳情若行
散文者故言表必依於宋是表正自得其體裁且
punctuated:
不一者，聖人同天下之分也。蓋至此，則天下之偏乎一、過不及乎一者，皆歸於聖人之一矣。而聖人盡倫立道之效，至於天地訢合，萬物昭蘇，橫四海，塞天地，施之後世，而無不一矣。《易》曰：「天下之動，貞夫一者也。」裁成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，一之至也。聖人與天地參矣，又如之何其可及也？嘗聞之：「聖可學乎？一爲要。」一者，無欲；無欲則靜虛動直。靜虛則明，而人倫之理洞然於吾心而無所蔽；動直則公，而人倫之理渾然於吾身而無所虧。勿助勿忘，兩忘俱化，是亦聖人之一也。孟子曰：「堯舜性之也。」人皆可以爲堯舜。噫！知堯舜之可爲，則知聖人之可學矣。

陳試

translation_en:
…that nothing remains outside this unity is the allotment the sage shares with all under Heaven. At this point, all those under Heaven who deviate from unity, overshoot it, or fall short of it return to the sage’s unity. The effects of the sage’s fulfilling human relationships and establishing the Way extend to Heaven and Earth joining in harmony and the myriad things flourishing anew. They reach across the Four Seas, fill Heaven and Earth, and extend to later generations, leaving nothing outside this unity. The Book of Changes says: “The movements of all under Heaven are made constant through unity.” To regulate and complete the Way of Heaven and Earth, and to assist what is fitting to them, is unity at its utmost. The sage thus stands alongside Heaven and Earth as a third. How, then, could anyone attain his level?

I have heard it said: “Can sagehood be learned? Unity is the essential thing.” Unity means freedom from desire. Without desire, one is empty in stillness and upright in action. Emptiness in stillness brings clarity, so that the principles of human relationships are fully illuminated within my mind, with nothing obscuring them. Uprightness in action brings impartiality, so that the principles of human relationships are wholly embodied in my person, with nothing lacking. Neither force their growth nor forget them; both injunctions are forgotten and together dissolve in transformation. This too is the sage’s unity. Mengzi said: “Yao and Shun possessed it by nature.” Everyone can become a Yao or a Shun. Ah! To understand that one can become a Yao or a Shun is to understand that sagehood can be learned.

Memorial

title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
善寫司馬忠愛之意錄之
考試官敎諭黃批莊重得告君之體
考試官學正林批一表佳甚
元祐元年某月某日尚書左僕射兼門下
侍郎臣司馬光謹以所撰十科舉士法
進呈者
運屬方隆國以多賢爲實士嚴始進禮無不
介而行在
人主之必求貴官人之有法臣光誠惶誠恐稽
===
首頓首竊以才難自昔器罕通方唐虞二
帝之間兼收九德稷契五人之輩各效一
官周家以三俊甄才漢法以四科辟士得
則丞相故事失則開元聖書蓋有能有不
能自天性之常分而無可無不可惟
人君之曲成矧當
繼體之初急在用人之際若皆求備何以獲周
彷徨於
付託之隆愈難其任反覆於圖惟之隙稍得其
punctuated:
善寫司馬忠愛之意，錄之。

考試官學正林批：一表佳甚。
元祐元年某月某日，尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎臣司馬光，謹以所撰十科舉士法進呈者：

…It also finely conveys Sima Guang’s loyal devotion and concern. Include it.
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Grave and dignified, it achieves the proper form for addressing the ruler.”
Examiner Lin, Director of Studies, comments: “An excellent memorial throughout.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of Yuanyou, your servant Sima Guang, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery, respectfully submits the regulations he has drafted for recommending men under ten categories:
As the fortunes of the age rise toward prosperity, the state takes an abundance of worthy men as its true substance. A scholar treats his first entry into service with solemn care; ritual requires an intermediary before he proceeds. Since the ruler must seek men out, what matters is having a method for appointing them. Your servant Guang, in utmost fear and trepidation, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows.
I humbly reflect that talent has been hard to find since antiquity, and few men possess capacities embracing every field. Under the two emperors, Yao and Shun, men possessing the nine virtues were all taken into service; Ji, Xie, and the others among the five each performed the duties of one office. The Zhou selected talent through the three classes of outstanding men; Han regulations recruited scholars under four categories. Successful practice is exemplified by the precedents of the chief councilor, unsuccessful practice by the imperial writing of the Kaiyuan era [?]. For men to possess some abilities and lack others is the normal distribution of natural endowments; but to treat no man as categorically acceptable or unacceptable depends upon the ruler’s nurturing each according to his particular capacities.
Especially now, at the beginning of your succession, when employing men is urgent, if perfection is demanded of everyone, how can all needs be met? title: 嘉靖二十八年廣東鄉試錄
text:
方瑣以科條具而列上自
表著欽賢之地曁
侍從補
袞之階一軍在將帥之身諸路以監司爲命
經術備
啓沃論思之用文學分
對揚潤色之司授計正辭非其人則莫理治
書閱獄得其情而後平冀收一網之功定
以十科之目構緣雲之厦屋杞梓兼裁航
===
治水之艅艎篙楫並御試諸其職能其官
乃命以官責在其人必有是斯能舉是歲
一官而三薦人無舉而不公自然耳目之
周坐致賢才之衆狐無粹白蓋有千金之
裘樂以大成必合八音之奏初爲此策有
與共圖咸謂可行故敢祈於
一鑒有如未盡亦不憚於再籌恭惟
○○○○
聖本生知
punctuated:
方，瑣以科條，具而列上：自表著欽賢之地，曁侍從補袞之階，一軍在將帥之身，諸路以監司爲命。經術備啓沃論思之用，文學分對揚潤色之司。授計正辭，非其人則莫理；治書閱獄，得其情而後平。冀收一網之功，定以十科之目。構緣雲之厦屋，杞梓兼裁；航治水之艅艎，篙楫並御。試諸其職，能其官，乃命以官；責在其人，必有是斯能舉是。歲一官而三薦人，無舉而不公，自然耳目之周，坐致賢才之衆。狐無粹白，蓋有千金之裘；樂以大成，必合八音之奏。初爲此策，有與共圖，咸謂可行，故敢祈於一鑒。有如未盡，亦不憚於再籌。恭惟
○○○○
聖本生知
translation_en:
…a method, setting it out in detailed regulations [?], fully enumerated and submitted above: from the ranks of the outer court, where worthy men are honored, to the attendant officials, whose duty is to remedy the sovereign’s shortcomings. An army depends upon its commander; the various circuits depend for their very life upon their surveillance commissioners. Learning in the classics supplies the means to enlighten the sovereign and deliberate upon affairs; literary accomplishment serves the several duties of responding to and proclaiming imperial commands and refining their expression. Entrusting financial accounts and setting official language aright cannot be properly managed without suitable men; handling documents and reviewing criminal cases can achieve fairness only after the facts have been ascertained. Hoping to gather all talent in a single net, I have established ten categories. To build a great hall reaching to the clouds, both qi and zi timber must be fashioned for use; to navigate a great vessel upon the waters [?], poles and oars must be employed together.

Test men in their duties, and only when they prove capable of an office appoint them to it. Responsibility rests with the individual: only one who possesses the requisite ability can carry out the corresponding task. Each year, let each official recommend three men, with no recommendation made unfairly. Naturally, the reach of our eyes and ears will become comprehensive, and a multitude of worthy and talented men will be gathered with ease. No fox is wholly white, yet a white fur robe worth a thousand pieces of gold can be made; to bring music to its full perfection, the sounds of all eight classes of instruments must be combined. When I first devised this proposal, others joined me in considering it, and all deemed it practicable. Thus I venture to pray that you will examine it.
